findings.validation: Full source-body assessment; no retained workflow executed.

findings.title: Generated metaskill leaves contradict the shared residual-evidence boundary
findings.finding: The shared verifier correctly says finite residual observations remain diagnostics regardless of count and general contraction needs a checked statement. Every generated leaf instead permits admission after three observed contractive runs. A before/after scalar drop is also not a metric contraction theorem, and zero-to-zero preservation need not be strict contraction.
findings.recommended_action: Make leaves defer to the shared finite-evidence ceiling, name the exact diagnostic and admitted domain, and remove unsupported contractive frontmatter. Prove any general preservation/decrease statement separately.
findings.validation: CHECK-049 constructs a function decreasing at three tested inputs and increasing at another.

findings.title: Historical meta traces omit the inputs required by their declared signatures
findings.finding: Three retained traces claim unary State, Receipt or Paper transformations but record inputs=[]. Each binds only an output path/hash and residual numbers, with no actual input/problem/producer/metric pin. Their internal count flag is false, but even reaching three would not repair the missing bindings or establish execution fidelity.
findings.recommended_action: Preserve historical bytes and mark these as unbound historical observations; require exact input/output/producer/metric bindings and replayable independent validation for new evidence.
findings.validation: Full source-body assessment; no retained workflow executed.

findings.title: Comment-purge helper can corrupt source and cross the advertised preservation boundary
findings.finding: The C/Rust block regex deletes comment-like substrings inside strings and merges adjacent tokens, while Python comment removal also strips meaningful shebang/encoding/type/licence directives. Test protection checks basename only, so files under tests may be rewritten. Recursive writes follow file symlinks and lack a root containment/custody transaction. Shared verifier promises preserved licence notices and tests.
findings.recommended_action: Disable destructive generic rewriting pending language-aware parsing, allowed-root/link checks, complete test/licence preservation, byte snapshots and reviewable atomic writes. A residual comment count must not substitute for semantic preservation.
findings.validation: CHECK-047/048 show exact string corruption/token merging and test-tree omission without touching source.

findings.title: Meta launchers can bind to an unrelated current working checkout
findings.finding: Every launcher accepts Path.cwd() with .git and .agents before its own ancestors, then prepends that root to sys.path and imports a shared CLI. Executing the retained script from another qualifying checkout can import a different implementation without pinning it.
findings.recommended_action: Anchor implementation discovery to the script/package or explicit verified repo root and record exact imported producer path/hash; do not let incidental CWD choose semantics.
findings.validation: Full source-body assessment; no retained workflow executed.

findings.title: Skew-information inequality fails for the stated arbitrary CPTP channel
findings.finding: Source defines I_rho(H)=Tr(rho H²)-Tr(sqrt(rho)Hsqrt(rho)H) and claims I_E(rho)(E(H))<=I_rho(H). Take rho=diag(1/3,2/3), H=P0, E(A)=A00 P0+A11 Pplus. Kraus K0=|0><0| and K1=|+><1| sum KdaggerK=I. E(H)=H, but E(rho)=[[2/3,1/3],[1/3,1/3]], so I grows from0 to1/15. Both states are positive definite. This is not the correctly transported tangent-vector monotonicity theorem.
findings.recommended_action: Remove or restrict this inequality with exact channel/observable hypotheses and proof; separate skew information from general monotone metric contraction. Retain this negative control.
findings.validation: CHECK-050 verifies complete channel/state/observable, positive square root identity and rational terms2/3-3/5=1/15.

findings.title: Closed overlap differences are incorrectly called pairwise agreement
findings.finding: Reference first defines omega=delta0(local observations), then calls delta1 omega=0 pairwise consistency. For local values0,1,2 on a triangle, edge differences1,1,-2 are nonzero but sum0. Such omega is already exact by definition; its closed-survivor branch cannot occur without changing the supplied data model. Nilpotence, closedness, exactness and agreement are distinct predicates.
findings.recommended_action: Define independent edge data when closed nonexact classes are intended; test delta0(local)=0 for agreement. Require image/kernel equality for exactness, not only d²=0. The skill phrase exact complexes with d²=0 may impose both, so do not treat its wording alone as a proved false implication.
findings.validation: CHECK-051/052 separate nilpotence from exactness and closedness from zero differences.

findings.title: Nonzero H1 group is not equivalent to missing global sections
findings.finding: Source asserts no global sections iff H1 is nonzero, including a Set-valued presheaf without an abelianization/support construction. Constant Q coefficients on a circle have H1=Q and many global constant sections. A particular contextuality obstruction class, empirical support and the whole cohomology group must not be identified.
findings.recommended_action: Specify empirical model, support/distribution extension problem, coefficient construction and distinguished obstruction class; state only the direction and completeness theorem actually justified.
findings.validation: CHECK-053 supplies explicit incidence matrix, rank2, H1 dimension1 and global zero section.

findings.title: Discrete Wigner expression lacks normalization and characteristic restriction
findings.finding: With the displayed phase-point convention, Tr A=1 and maximally mixed rho=I/d gives the displayed W=1/d at d² points, summing to d. Standard normalized W needs an additional1/d. The exponent also uses inverse2 for every prime d, which is undefined in characteristic2.
findings.recommended_action: State odd-prime/odd-prime-power domain and consistent displacement/phase-point/Wigner conventions; test total mass and marginals before using contextuality conclusions.
findings.validation: CHECK-057 computes the d=3 maximally mixed normalization failure.

findings.title: General-poset and cross-domain obstruction formulas omit required structure
findings.finding: Galois connections yield an upper closure operator, but subtraction c-gamma(alpha(c)) is undefined for general posets. Truncation A->||A||n is a unit map, not generally an inclusion. Displayed lifting problem also asks a map X->E to extend f:A->B without specifying a lift on A or base extension on X.
findings.recommended_action: Keep the valid order closure statement; admit extra additive/metric structure before a numerical residual. Repair types and local-coefficient/simplicity hypotheses before claiming universal obstruction unification.
findings.validation: Full source body reviewed; no retained workflow executed.

findings.title: SUSY note promotes determinant equality and superalgebra into missing guarantees
findings.finding: Equality det J=det DF does not force a positive determinant; superalgebra {Q,Qdagger}=2H alone does not force every state to be annihilated by Q. A zero-energy state premise would be needed. The note supplies no boundary-map bridge from this algebra to simplicial nilpotence and lists3D Pachner counts under a4D heading.
findings.recommended_action: Require explicit admitted complexes, determinant sign/domain conditions, zero-energy constraint and chain-map proof; use dimension-correct moves and treat sampled positivity as finite evidence.
findings.validation: CHECK-054/055/056 provide negative determinant, two-state supercharge and facet-count controls.

findings.title: Schema conformer upgrades evidence labels and drops valid quoted aliases
findings.finding: The mechanical MANUAL->VERIFIED migration map claims test/source verification without running or binding any verification. Alias regex recognizes double quoting only, so a valid single-quoted gt alias is dropped. Delimiter scanning can treat a later Markdown horizontal rule as frontmatter.
findings.recommended_action: Keep evidence status unchanged unless fresh owner evidence is supplied; parse actual anchored frontmatter losslessly, preserve aliases and original bytes, and generate reviewable changes before writes.
findings.validation: CHECK-058 isolates the actual alias regex; source inspection establishes unconditional status rewrite.

findings.title: Quantum/gauge unification confuses conditional, geometric and dynamical claims
findings.finding: Nonzero curvature need not give nonidentity holonomy on every chosen loop (an abelian flux2pi is a counterexample). One amplitude vector sqrt(probability) exp(i phase) does not encode every mixed density operator. P rho P is unnormalized postselection unless divided by its probability. Failure of a time-homogeneous semigroup does not alone prove non-Markovian memory; a time-dependent unitary propagator can be CP-divisible.
findings.recommended_action: Name the admitted bundle/local trivialization, loop, instrument and conditioning convention; distinguish pure-state encoding, mixed states, homogeneous semigroups and CP-divisibility. Supply actual cochain maps rather than assigning C1 by label.
findings.validation: Full source body reviewed; no retained workflow executed.

findings.title: Quotient verifier lacks the laws named by its stages
findings.finding: Slot colours alone do not establish planar associativity; the quotient relation and congruence needed for well-defined composition are unspecified, and a Convention parameter appears outside the declared colour inventory. Three-run contraction wording repeats the shared-specification contradiction.
findings.recommended_action: Declare operations, identities/composition, quotient relation, congruence and associativity witnesses. Separate type checking, finite execution and universal invariants; defer to the stronger shared meta boundary.
findings.validation: Full source body reviewed; no retained workflow executed.

findings.title: Lifecycle registers disagree on admitted versus pending skills
findings.finding: Current register labels four entries307--310 pending review although the same skill names occur admitted in archived entries302--305; the recommended queue says none through306. README inert-draft wording also differs from promotion claims. These are incompatible snapshots without an event-bound lifecycle record.

findings.title: Encyclopedia extraction excludes flat programme papers as overviews
findings.finding: The depth-only overview predicate returns true for every published/<programme>/<paper>.md, despite the discovery helper explicitly accepting flat files distinct from the programme overview. Such rows are removed before extraction. A real indexed PO001 path has exactly this shape.

findings.title: Frontmatter parser silently discards dependency items and duplicate keys
findings.finding: If an inline list contains any quote, parser extracts quoted values only and drops unquoted items; duplicate keys overwrite without an error. A missing entries directory also returns an empty clean result. These can make schema consistency look stronger than the admitted source population.

findings.title: Historical extraction dispositions are not bound to statement bodies
findings.finding: Disposition reuse keys contain kind,label,name,occurrence and match source paths, but omit statement/proof/body digests. A theorem body can change while the disposition remains. The target manifest is also read unconditionally after same-source lookup. Printed parity-gate language is not an executable proof or verification check.

findings.finding: emit_indexes and several manifest writes/prunes occur before missing declared GT sources are returned as failure. No transaction protects the generated set. --check is nonwriting but its byte-identical description is stronger than its newline-normalized text comparison.

findings.title: Type-equality checker rejects safe generated equality and accepts guard text
findings.finding: Frozen dataclasses already generate exact-class equality; absence of explicit __eq__ is not cross-type vulnerability. Scanner instead accepts a guard substring anywhere in unparsed source, including a docstring, without checking control flow. Dotted decorators and missing target populations are also omitted.

findings.title: Isolation and architecture PASS messages exceed their predicates
findings.finding: Isolation helper only ensures CWD/scratch exists, creating it if missing. Architecture discovery only includes engine* and the_symbol_game roots, excluding pfp, and never comprehensively checks inward imports. Filename/class heuristics, adapter exemptions and ignored syntax errors can pass unchecked behavior.

findings.title: Inspector obstruction and tautology rules contain false mathematical premises
findings.finding: Zero d0/d1 does not force Phi1 zero: distance of omega=1 from image(d0)={0} is1. Valid exact repair on a graph needs no2-faces. A Boolean literal returned from a data-dependent match arm can compute a nonconstant predicate and is not intrinsically tautological. Universal veto rules would reject valid mechanisms.
findings.recommended_action: Specify actual quotient metric and admitted cell dimensions; judge dependence and falsifiability semantically. Keep real residual/source binding requirements while dropping false universal syntactic conditions.

findings.title: TDVP follow-on recipe omits subgradient and tangent transport conditions
findings.finding: The full displayed dual certificate has norm bound, saturation and tangent annihilation and is useful. However sign(Q)+P_Tperp(V) with only a norm check need not saturate Q. Contractivity of a channel alone does not imply distance to a fixed tangent is nonincreasing; a Hadamard channel sends Z in span(Z) to X outside it.
findings.recommended_action: Check all displayed dual conditions and feasibility; treat argmin as potentially set-valued. Transport or prove invariance of the tangent when invoking channel contraction.
findings.validation: CHECK-068/069 separate the valid full witness from invalid shortcuts.

findings.title: Normal-form CDC repair omits deterministic ties and projected dependencies
findings.finding: ROW_NUMBER ordering only by event_timestamp and sequence_num leaves two same-key events with different payloads unordered. The recursive BCNF sketch also needs the implied FD projection on each component, not merely original FDs whose attributes happen to fit.
findings.recommended_action: Admit unique immutable event ordering or refuse tied conflicting payloads. Specify projected dependency computation and distinguish finite-instance checks from all-schema semantics.
findings.validation: CHECK-070 exhibits two admissible tied winners; BCNF limitation is an algorithm specification obligation.

findings.title: Blanket Python healthy-pattern rewrites can widen strict contracts
findings.finding: The review rubric recommends isTrue/isFalse→truthiness and treats isinstance as an exact-type substitute elsewhere. Strict admission of True differs from admitting1 or a nonempty false string; exact numeric validation may intentionally exclude arbitrary subclasses as well as bool. Detector-zero is not behavioral equivalence or unique repair.
findings.recommended_action: Make semantic carrier/contract preservation a precondition of each rewrite and test wrong-type cases; keep syntax/style diagnostics separate from correctness.
findings.validation: CHECK-072 shows the accepted input set changes.

findings.title: Anti-mock snippet cannot justify its own clean-scan claim
findings.finding: Embedded scanner only finds ImportFrom nodes with module unittest.mock. It does not implement the advertised facade, tautology, monkeypatch, alias-import or Rust analysis, yet claims a clean scan supports their absence.
findings.recommended_action: Report exact predicates/language/population and implement separately tested rules before broad absence claims.
findings.validation: Full body review; no retained owner invocation.

findings.title: Paper-reader speed and fixture metrics are presented as broad verification
findings.finding: Mandatory1-to-1 mapping between each claim and Python/test/notebook/Lean ignores many-to-many and noncomputational claims. Absolute1e-12 numerical agreement and finite parameter stress tests do not certify prose theorems. Report template hardcodes100 percent and sustained-and-verified language without evidence binding.
findings.recommended_action: Separate usability timing, mapping completeness, finite checks and formal proof. Compute each actual denominator/status and bind artifacts, premises and checker results; use relations rather than forced bijections.
findings.validation: Full body review; no retained owner invocation.

findings.title: Scanner mode combination silently disables both rule families
findings.finding: CLI permits --arch-only and --pitfalls-only simultaneously; project sets AST rules empty and skips architecture pass. Parseable bad source then receives no active-rule findings, and console says codebase satisfies active rules.
findings.recommended_action: Make flags mutually exclusive or define one explicit mode enum; record enabled rule IDs and refuse zero-rule scans.
findings.validation: CHECK-073 evaluates the exact guards.

findings.title: Scanner dependency and test classification miss ordinary production cases
findings.finding: ImportedSymbol drops relative depth and dependency rule resolves only module, ignoring imported name and relative flag; from..import infrastructure therefore has an empty resolution key. Any filename containing test, including latest.py, is classified as test and exempted from architecture/assert checks. source_roots configuration is unused in package mapping.
findings.recommended_action: Resolve imports relative to actual packages/source roots, preserve depth and imported submodules, and use precise test patterns/explicit inventory rather than substring exemptions.
findings.validation: CHECK-074/076 demonstrate both false-negative paths.

findings.title: Noqa recognition treats string contents as suppression directives
findings.finding: Both suppression helpers regex-match raw lines without tokenizing comments. A production assert with message containing # noqa suppresses itself despite no actual comment. Policy exceptions therefore arise accidentally from string data.
findings.recommended_action: Use tokenize comment tokens with declared line scope and record every suppression in the receipt; fail malformed codes rather than dropping them.
findings.validation: CHECK-075 uses an in-memory assert with a literal message.

findings.title: Test runner does not propagate all failed prerequisites
findings.finding: Collection, mechanical gate and focused tests always execute in sequence regardless of earlier failure. Malformed gate stdout at exit0 creates GATE_ERROR but still labels gatePASS; final exit ignores collection failure. Subprocesses have no timeout and receipt discards raw outputs and exact argv, limiting replay/custody.
findings.recommended_action: Stop or explicitly isolate dependent execution after failed prerequisites, make parse/schema/findings failures fail closed, include collection in aggregate status and bind exact argv/full outputs/source/config with bounded timeouts.
findings.validation: CHECK-078 reproduces status logic on synthetic values without subprocess execution.

findings.title: Quality gate can pass unavailable targets and ineffective raises restrictions
findings.finding: File discovery silently ignores missing paths and pytest node IDs, yielding zero-file success. A match=None AST node is accepted as a match restriction. Presence of dead/nested assertions or arbitrary raises-named calls also satisfies no-assertion checks, which is consistent only with the stated narrow syntactic ceiling.
findings.recommended_action: Refuse unresolved/zero required populations and either resolve pytest selectors to files or accept explicit paths only. Validate effective match values and keep behavioral adequacy separate.
findings.validation: CHECK-077 demonstrates None bypass; other limits follow full body review.

findings.title: Scanner documentation promises a larger active rule set and stricter exit than supplied
findings.finding: Default registry contains24 AST rule classes plus three architecture rules; ViewDoesNotImportOrmRule exists but is not registered. README says findings imply nonzero exit, but controller returns0 for warning-only results. Several50-item rubric checks are not implemented and clean scan is not comprehensive review.
findings.recommended_action: Publish the exact active predicate inventory and severity exit policy, register/test intended missing rules, and retain README no-proof ceiling.
findings.validation: CHECK-079 records actual24 names; source inspection establishes registration/exit behavior.

findings.title: Commit/reveal snippet treats unavailable or empty population as success
findings.finding: Verification runs only if the manifest exists, missing cases defaults to an empty list, and comparisons use assert. Missing evidence therefore produces no refusal and optimized Python removes hash comparisons; no timestamp/precommitment or blinding follows from digest equality alone.
findings.recommended_action: Require explicit nonempty exact case inventory, strict manifest shape/duplicates/path rules and unconditional mismatch errors; retain old commitment versions and independent chronology.
findings.validation: CHECK-086; source review of assertion and defaults.

findings.title: Paper extraction omits mathematical content from claim-statement bindings
findings.finding: Display-math branches continue before appending to an active claim buffer, so changing a displayed equation can leave claim statement hash/UUID unchanged. Claim-header lines also continue before inline extraction; numeric inline formulas are excluded and embedded display dollars are additionally parsed as inline. Exhaustive typed inventory is not achieved.
findings.recommended_action: Use one explicit grammar with disjoint formula spans; bind claim raw spans including displayed equations and preserve title/type/occurrences. Report rejected/unclosed syntax and extraction coverage rather than exhaustive labels.
findings.validation: CHECK-081/082 show duplicate classification, numeric exclusion and unchanged statement despite changed equation.

findings.title: Byte anchors describe newline-normalized text instead of source bytes
findings.finding: Markdown and TeX use read_text with universal newline conversion, then re-encode normalized strings to compute offsets. On CRLF files every preceding line shifts byte positions; location hashes contain no raw file digest to resolve representation ambiguity. Existing tests only check nonempty ranges.
findings.recommended_action: Read raw bytes, define decoding/newline representation explicitly, compute anchors against that representation and include raw source digest; test exact slicing with CRLF and Unicode.
findings.validation: CHECK-080 demonstrates reported2 versus actual3 for second-line start.

findings.title: ZIP checksum cross-check verifies names and can pass without bound modules
findings.finding: Digest columns in SHA256SUMS/MANIFEST are ignored; arbitrary suffix matches satisfy required names without unique rooted members or byte checks. Ancillary checksum/document requirements make required nonempty even when code/proof bindings are absent, bypassing advertised no-bindings refusal. Whole ZIP hash is useful custody but does not repair these missing checks.
findings.recommended_action: Separate binding presence from ancillary membership; validate digest syntax and each exact uniquely rooted regular member against expected bytes, reject duplicates/ambiguous paths, and name membership-only receipts accurately.
findings.validation: CHECK-083/084; existing source test accepts abc12345/def67890 as checksum columns.

findings.title: Paper coverage links are unverified ledger associations
findings.finding: Ledger entries become code/Lean bindings without file existence/hash/declaration/type checks; fallback number matching can associate a different claim kind. Regex Lean declaration names and inherited formula bindings are counted as coverage. Test fixture uses a True theorem and a pass function, so coverage is association coverage, not proof/implementation adequacy.
findings.recommended_action: Rename fields to association coverage or validate exact source/statement/premise bindings separately; preserve missing/ambiguous references and never infer proof from a path/name.
findings.validation: Full source inspection; no Lean/runtime replay or theorem correspondence claim.

findings.title: Identity CONSISTENT conflates missing metadata with verified parity
findings.finding: Missing author/version/date/PDF produces no mismatch; creator/author checks merely contain Carroll and PDF author flag is not enforced. Different full author names can pass, and fallback version1.0.0 is synthesized. Pydantic shape bounds do not enforce count/hash/key/reference consistency.
findings.recommended_action: Use explicit unavailable/partial/consistent/mismatch states, compare declared complete identities and validate manifest relationships/digests independently.
findings.validation: CHECK-085 covers all-missing identity case; model invariants inspected in full.

findings.title: Strict Boolean recipe rejects every Boolean
findings.finding: isinstance(v,bool) and not isinstance(v,(int,str)) rejects True and False since bool subclasses int. This normative recipe cannot admit any valid Boolean record.
findings.recommended_action: Use type(v) is bool or isinstance(v,bool) and test both valid Booleans plus integers/strings; use explicit exceptions rather than assert for production.
findings.validation: CHECK-087 evaluates all relevant finite examples.

findings.title: Skill root path recipe has an off-by-one parent index
findings.finding: The stated .agents/skills/name/scripts/file.py hierarchy has repository root at file.parents[4]; parents[3] is .agents. The os.path dirname plus four ascents alternative is correct, so the supposedly equivalent recipes disagree.
findings.recommended_action: Use script-relative verified root resolution and test the actual installed hierarchy; do not mix dirname ascent count with Path.parents index.
findings.validation: CHECK-088 gives exact paths.

findings.title: Cochain dimension and coordinate bounds need explicit representative restrictions
findings.finding: For a3-cycle without2-faces every standard edge is closed and has quotient l1 distance1. These raw surviving cochains span dimension3, but beta1=1; equality applies to quotient classes or chosen complementary representatives. Positive observer weights and quotient descent likewise do not bound arbitrary raw gauge coordinates: d0=[-1,1], c=cprime=100 has quotient norm0.
findings.recommended_action: State whether survivors are classes, harmonic/optimal residuals or raw cochains. Require norm-bounded representative and actual per-observer descent before using coordinate inequality; keep quotient and representative norms distinct.
findings.validation: CHECK-089 gives primal/dual witnesses and ranks; CHECK-090 gives exact coordinate counterexample.

findings.title: Trace-distance product formula omits real normalized domain
findings.finding: The product one-half norm(a-b) norm(a+b) computes rank-one trace distance for normalized real vectors. It fails for allowed-looking complex unit vectors a=1,b=i: both densities are[1] yet product1. Unnormalized vectors also need scale treatment.
findings.recommended_action: Declare real unit-sphere domain or use phase-invariant complex formula with normalization/zero checks; distinguish lift fibers from signed cochain orientation.
findings.validation: CHECK-091 records exact unit-phase counterexample.

findings.title: Dual flow statement reverses complementary slackness and closure statement is overbroad
findings.finding: Source says nonzero edge flow requires zero residual. In weighted l1 duality nonzero residual requires y=w*sign(r), while zero residual permits any bounded feasible dual coordinate. Source also says norms cannot determine closure; a correctly computed definite exact norm(d1r)=0 is exactly closure, although norm(r) alone cannot determine exactness and unbound scalar claims are not certificates.
findings.recommended_action: Correct signed saturation/free-zero-coordinate conditions and distinguish actual computed exact norm from an unverified scalar or seminorm. Preserve actual operators/certificates in receipts.
findings.validation: CHECK-092 exhibits primal=dual=1 with nonzero r,y; CHECK-093 states exact norm equivalence.

findings.title: Encoding repair policy identifies valid mathematical Unicode as corruption
findings.finding: Documentation manager lists valid Phi, lambda, arrows and middle dots as mojibake and mandates automatic repair; lint policy additionally standardizes to dollar delimiters then says to flag/replace those same delimiters. These instructions can rewrite sound mathematical source without evidence of corruption.
findings.recommended_action: Require byte/decoding diagnosis and explicit before/after provenance; preserve valid Unicode and state one noncontradictory supported delimiter grammar.
findings.validation: Full source-body comparison; no source rewritten.

findings.title: Rule corpus contains mutually conflicting canonical contracts
findings.finding: Same architecture rule forbids reexports then requires public __all__ reexports; triad manager manifests are mandated while persona manifests are permanently retired; exact rational JSON is p/q-only in one rule but unit denominators must omit slash in another. Historical and scoped exceptions need explicit precedence to avoid incompatible gates. Publication rules additionally require and retire claim ledgers/maps, require and prohibit AuthorityEffect in manuscripts, and both mandate dated ZIP names and ban calendar dates in deliverables.
findings.recommended_action: Version and scope rules by current owner/profile; retain historical definitions as historical and make policy conflict an explicit refusal rather than automatic source mutation.
findings.validation: Full text comparison; related F052 policy conflicts preserved.

findings.title: Absent constructive instance is incorrectly equated with uninhabitability
findings.finding: A rule says an axiom set without an exhibited constructive inhabitant is an uninstantiable specification. Absence of an exhibited instance is absence of positive evidence, not proof that no instance exists. Requiring an instance for promotion is a defensible policy, with a different logical claim.
findings.recommended_action: Label instance status unestablished/unavailable, reserve inconsistent or uninhabitable for a proof, and distinguish by-construction subtype theorems from external adequacy.
findings.validation: Direct logical distinction; no external formal library replay.

findings.title: Set-plus-count exhaustion predicate assumes unique identifiers
findings.finding: Equal sets and equal list lengths can pass when duplicate multiplicities differ: declared[a,a,b] and checked[a,b,b]. Exact inventory/candidate binding requires unique IDs or multiset agreement, not counts and sets alone.
findings.recommended_action: Validate unique identifiers at ingress or compare canonical multisets while binding each checked result to candidate bytes.
findings.validation: CHECK-094; bounded predicate issue, not a claim current owners admit duplicate IDs.

findings.title: Rational squared lengths do not force every deficit to be irrational
findings.finding: Mathematical hygiene says rational positive squared edge lengths yield transcendental angles/deficits and delta notin Q. A flat Euclidean triangulated square fan has squared lengths1,2 and deficit0. Nonzero angle/deficit hypotheses cannot be omitted.
findings.recommended_action: State the precise nonzero algebraic-exponential hypotheses and allow exactly flat rational-zero deficits; retain interval exclusions only for claimed nonzero curvature.
findings.validation: CHECK-096 exact flat fan construction.

findings.title: Epsilon-set ranking differs from strict primary priority in the same rule
findings.finding: The global epsilon policy first admits candidates within epsilon of minimal discrete score, then selects near-minimal Xi, so it may choose a strictly worse primary score. This conflicts with the nearby strict lexicographic priority requirement even though it avoids pairwise tolerance cycles.
findings.recommended_action: Declare two distinct policies with explicit selection contract or apply exact lexicographic ordering; bind policy/epsilon into receipts and tests.
findings.validation: CHECK-095 selects B(primary1/2,Xi0) over A(primary0,Xi100) at epsilon1.

findings.title: Finite-QM workflow imports APIs absent from current bridge owner
findings.finding: The workflow imports evaluate_state_observables, verify_exact_state_with_engine, evaluate_state_fidelity and evaluate_bures_geometry from engine_bridge; its Born/Gleason and tomography bridge helpers are also absent from the complete current module. Present APIs supply exact-to-diagnostic conversion and interval enclosures, not the documented bidirectional workflow. Existing quantum review distinguishes actual finite tomography from physical/Born selection.
findings.recommended_action: Update examples to actual owning APIs and declare one-way conversion; bind any restoration/migration to exact source and bounded tests. Preserve earlier recipes as history rather than claim current executability.
findings.validation: CHECK-097 plus full156-line owner inspection and pinned prior QP-C027/context; no compilation.

findings.title: Mutation equivalence guidance promotes small-case enumeration beyond its carrier
findings.finding: The custody skill says prove equivalence by exhaustive search over small cases. This proves only that finite population unless it exhausts the admitted domain or a reduction theorem connects all cases. Two integer functions can agree on0..100 and differ at101.
findings.recommended_action: State the complete finite domain or supply a mathematical reduction/universal proof; otherwise label mutant apparently equivalent on tested cases and keep unchecked remainder.
findings.validation: CHECK-098 supplies bounded-versus-unbounded counterexample.

findings.title: Paper zero-curvature preflight requires stronger exactness than claimed
findings.finding: The preflight requires both Phi1=0 and Gamma2=0 for papers asserting zero curvature. Closed nonexact cochains have Gamma2=0 and Phi1>0, so a valid zero-curvature claim would be refused by this declared rule. Exact repair and closedness are different obligations.
findings.recommended_action: Select certificates for the actual claim: closure d1omega=0 versus exactness omega in image(d0), and require valid dual/primal checks only for declared optimization statements.
findings.validation: Existing CHECK-089 supplies exact3-cycle witnesses Phi1=1,Gamma2=0; this is rule inconsistency, not an executed preflight failure.

findings.title: Artifact custody advice improperly upgrades declarations and frequent conventions into laws
findings.finding: Custody skill says artifact epistemic declarations outrank plans and self-rules should be enforced biconditionally by default; it also calls98percent conventions undocumented invariants. A source declaration can be wrong, one-way implication cannot be silently reversed, and frequency does not establish normative scope. Its later advice that verdicts require recomputation correctly limits the earlier rhetoric.
findings.recommended_action: Preserve declarations as source claims, resolve ownership/version and actual checks independently, and never strengthen logical direction or infer universal rules from frequencies.
findings.validation: Full-body logical review; no source/corpus mutation or claim that the specific historical examples are false.

findings.title: Sprint lifecycle declarations conflict and require their own future outputs
findings.finding: Retrospective pre-gate requires retrospective and VP briefing artifacts before retrospective; VP briefing requires its own briefing before evaluation. Planning supplies three documents but review demands eight including future completion/retro. Evidence roots disagree across manager/review/execution, commitment is soft in538 but hard in541, and deprecated improve-autoskill still has a required hash. No single literal first-run state machine can satisfy all these requirements without undefined placeholders/precedence.
findings.recommended_action: Choose one versioned artifact/state contract, distinct creation/completion states and canonical roots; migrate historical recipes explicitly and test first-run, exception and cleanup transitions.
findings.validation: CHECK-101 finite prerequisite cycle plus complete cross-file review. Actual hosts may implement different precedence; no orchestrator run.

findings.title: Sprint parsing loses or rejects supported cleanup identities
findings.finding: Both planning and review derive sprint_number using branch.split("-")[1], so sprint-108-0 becomes108 and targets the parent sprint. Explicit108-0 instead reaches int(sprint_number), which raises ValueError. The advertised cleanup hierarchy is therefore not represented by these examples.
findings.recommended_action: Treat sprint identity as an opaque validated string; preserve the entire suffix, and use a separately declared numeric database key when required.
findings.validation: CHECK-099 reproduces both exact expressions without invoking workflow.

findings.title: Displayed hard gates can accept empty evidence or return successful shell status after refusal
findings.finding: Planning artifact gate uses test-f only and merely echoes HARD BLOCK on failure, without exit1; its branch ends in successful echo. Review also uses existence rather than content despite a later all-documents-have-content condition. Completion predicate accepts any text containing two section names, including a zero-story zero-result document. Other manual instructions are stronger, so the snippets do not implement the claimed composite gate.
findings.recommended_action: Implement explicit nonzero refusal, typed required nonempty artifacts, source/task/result binding and unknown/error branches. Keep presence, structural and executed-verification states distinct.
findings.validation: CHECK-100 demonstrates exact header predicate; shell exit behavior follows the displayed echo-only branch, no shell execution claimed.

findings.title: Web-edit audit compares sprint branch to itself and cannot establish UI origin
findings.finding: The recipe selects sprint-{N}..HEAD. On that sprint branch at its own tip this is empty, omitting every sprint commit. Noreply author and at-most-two files identify neither GitHub UI origin nor bypassed CI; comment mentions no GPG signature but code never checks one. Recursive VETO grep similarly counts mentions rather than distinct events.
findings.recommended_action: Bind a recorded sprint base and reviewed head; inspect provider event/CI metadata if UI origin matters, otherwise label only the heuristic. Count structured event IDs rather than text mentions.
findings.validation: CHECK-102 exact revision-reachability model; no network or Git mutation/replay.

findings.title: Garden/count pairs do not diagnose or detect all colour drift
findings.finding: The census skill says pairing operation count with substitution count identifies size change versus colour drift. Distinct colour assignments can have equal operation/substitution counts: A:X→X,B:Y→Y admits AA and BB; A:X→X,B:X→Y admits AA and BA. Both counts are(2,2) while the wiring relation changes. Even when counts move they do not uniquely identify cause.
findings.recommended_action: Bind full operation identities/colours and the composable relation or its canonical source digest; use counts as diagnostics and preserve valid exact fixture/population assertions.
findings.validation: CHECK-103 enumerates all four unary pairs in each2-operation garden.

findings.title: Uncalled-module limitations incorrectly claim dynamic imports only under-report
findings.finding: The skill correctly admits stem/dynamic-import limitations, then says both failure modes are toward silence. A static test import plus a production importlib.import_module call produces test-only static importers although production is wired: an over-report. Static graph absence cannot establish runtime unreachability.
findings.recommended_action: Describe both false-positive and false-negative modes; require caller/entrypoint/plugin review before declaring a module unwired, and distinguish static references from actual reachable execution.
findings.validation: CHECK-104 parses complete independent code strings only; external operations owner not rerun.

findings.title: Missing declared falsifier does not imply unfalsifiable acceptance criterion
findings.finding: The gate auditor says every implementation satisfies a criterion naming no falsifier. Build success or a test predicate can fail without a separately written Decisive mutation field; a syntax mutation is an immediate counterexample. The later diagnostic-only count disclaimer is correct but does not justify the earlier equivalence.
findings.recommended_action: Report missing explicit falsification documentation separately from actual falsifiability and semantic adequacy; inspect/test the real predicate before saying nothing can turn it red.
findings.validation: CHECK-105 parses valid/invalid Python source to show a concrete falsifier without a named declaration.

findings.title: Publication language sweeps cannot certify total mathematical honesty
findings.finding: Anti-DIME bans proves and mathematical/common terms such as Primal Dual and Quarantine, while its own verdict guarantees100percent verified/honest materials. Generic wording controls can reject valid mathematical statements and still miss false claims. Public-claim statuses also overlap: a fully proved Lean implication under explicit analytic hypotheses is both MECHANIZED and HYP_GATED unless precedence is declared.
findings.recommended_action: Separate mathematical result status, premise scope, editorial style and publication authorization; declare status precedence or independent axes. Emit scoped reviewed findings rather than100percent truth certification and narrow lexical bans by context.

findings.assessment: ResearcherSwarm.dispatch reserves and permits PENDING, then sends; settlement/reconciliation happens afterward. Merge observes only the subsequently pending roles and breaks/skips when quorum, cap or other transition advances, leaving already executed replies outside run custody. The helper omits drive_teamwork executor/version gate, and future exceptions propagate before merge. Its dictionary reference helper is sequential and shallow-copies nested state, allowing callback mutation to leak between reviewers.

Unmatched claims become false alarms without independent refutation. candidate_reviewer_claims accumulates across build/repair because _v3_produced does not clear it, so later candidate checks can credit old claims. findings.title: Yardstick input admission and promotion labels exceed the statistical evidence.

L3 promotion compares two caller yields without sample/custody/checker evidence; infinity promotes ADMITTED_OPERAND. Thompson uses max(1,count), not prior+count; resets its RNG each call, treats zero cost as1 and negative cost as1e-6. These are declared heuristic policies, not established Bayesian learning or admission.

findings.title: Legacy directory custody hash has ambiguous path/content framing before mirror deletion.
findings.assessment: _dir_tree_sha256 concatenates each relative filename and raw contents without lengths or separators. A one-file tree a:"bc" and ab:"c" encode identical bytes. The same digest guards shutil.rmtree of a mirror, so hash equality need not imply equal path-to-byte populations. This is an encoding collision, not a SHA-256 collision.

The concrete checker may bind these correctly; this is a missing use-case boundary check, not a demonstrated production native bypass. Reopening can append a second genesis and failed writes can leave memory/disk divergent. The stronger genealogy store separately rereads and validates its chain; its guarantees cannot be transferred to this sink.

findings.title: Mutable antibody/catalog state has path and stale-admission hazards.
findings.assessment: Legacy catalog/pharmacy helpers form paths from unvalidated antibody identifiers. Default antibody cache is loaded once and can miss external revocation; recording candidates can overwrite existing status. Cemetery candidate publication uses read-modify-write so atomic replace alone does not prevent overwriting a concurrent admission. Newer typed admission paths remain stronger and must not be conflated.

findings.title: Scheduler completion and swarm echo helpers do not measure actual task progress.
findings.assessment: finish_bout derives statuses/routes from supplied completion rather than task evidence and emits changed_state1 for synthetic traversal. run_swarm helpers include a synchronous echo implementation with an infinite_timeout label whose timeout is unused. These can demonstrate choreography, but are not bounded worker execution or measured workflow success.

findings.title: Request value-object equality and hashing use incompatible representations.
findings.assessment: carrier_context equality uses ordinary dict equality, where {x:1} equals {x:True}; hash converts values to strings, which differ. Nested mutable dicts also undermine stable hashes of frozen dataclasses. Equal values can have unequal hashes and later mutate under the same object identity.
findings.limits: Source/body review; no end-to-end native or provider execution.
findings.next_action: Choose immutable canonical typed context or make the value object unhashable; define exact equality over the same representation used for hashing.

findings.title: Research HTTP identity and output path fields are caller claims, not authentication or confinement.
findings.assessment: The HTTP facade accepts operator identity in requests and constructs storage/export paths from caller fields without a demonstrated authentication/confinement boundary in this owner. Native state policy checks cannot establish who supplied those fields. Treat the facade as a trusted local tool unless an outer authenticated service explicitly binds them.
findings.limits: No HTTP server/request executed; no claim of a currently internet-exposed endpoint.
findings.next_action: Document trusted-local scope or add explicit authenticated identity and root-confined output paths before exposing the facade.

findings.title: The cochain CLI reads a different argument attribute from the one its parser defines.
findings.assessment: The run path accesses parsed.core while the parser defines --omega without a matching core destination. AttributeError is not caught by the surrounding ValueError handler, so the intended finite carrier path fails before evaluation.
findings.limits: Source inspection only; CLI was not invoked because its composition can load native/provider owners.

findings.title: Mutation manifest framing admits an exact prehash ambiguity.
findings.assessment: The path/action/old/new/content sequence is NUL-delimited, but RepoPath admits NUL and CREATE leaves old digest unrestricted. Distinct records (path a\0CREATE, old empty) and (path a, old CREATE\0), with the same CREATE action and valid new/content digests, encode byte-for-byte identically. This defeats canonical record identity before SHA-256; no cryptographic collision is needed.
findings.limits: A constructor-level witness; real filesystem NUL refusal can block later I/O. No filesystem mutation or historical receipt failure was shown. This is analogous to, but a distinct owner from, prior OAR-F11.
findings.next_action: Reject separators/control characters in every admitted field or use an injective length-prefixed/closed canonical encoding; enforce unused-field emptiness and recheck the full structured record.

findings.title: N1 lease verification does not bind the presented grant to stored scope and expiry.
findings.assessment: Verification compares ID, owner, epoch and only a lower-fence condition, then checks the presented expiry. A same-ID/owner/epoch record with a larger fence and later expiry passes after the stored grant expired; expanded path/resource/worktree scope is never compared. The independent finite control makes that difference explicit. Grant/revoke keys also precede Identifier normalization.
findings.limits: No original registry or real authority boundary executed. External unforgeable issuance/opaque handles could prevent presented-record substitution, but are not established in this owner. In-memory data are not durable atomic fencing.
findings.next_action: Verify exact stored lease identity and all scope/time fields, reject any unexpected fence, normalize keys before registration, and bind effect execution to durable atomic current-grant checks.

findings.title: N10 admission can exceed its ceiling when candidate IDs repeat.
findings.assessment: Conflict admission counts dictionary keys. The skeleton stores each accepted write set by candidate ID but appends every accepted record. Twenty repeated-ID disjoint-path records pass a ceiling of two while the map contains one key. Exact string overlap also admits parent/child directory path sets unless the population is restricted to canonical leaf files.
findings.limits: Only the admission fragment was reconstructed. No retained skeleton, random license issuance, Git or concurrent execution was run. Distinct identities and file-only write sets are sufficient additional preconditions for these particular controls.
findings.next_action: Require unique candidate identities before admission; count actual active work records; define whether scopes are canonical files or hierarchical regions and use the appropriate overlap relation.

findings.title: Qualification scenarios supply their own observations and stage completion labels.
findings.assessment: N1 appends lease/binding/landing/disposal/pruning states without the corresponding effects, using fixed epochs and expected blobs as default observations. N2 issues a refreshed license after a comment asserting fresh evidence without running a checker. N4 records counters without asserting expected scenario outcomes. N10 fabricates head strings, defaults missing observations to promises, and returns is_successful=True even for no admitted candidates. Receipt digests omit much of the input/content population.
findings.limits: Useful synthetic choreography remains; N10 explicitly disclaims full production DoD. These files are separate from prior OAR-F21 qualification DTOs and OAR-F23 scheduler fixtures. No historical outcome is inferred false merely because this source is a harness.
findings.next_action: Label the results as synthetic predicate scenarios; make observations mandatory for operational qualification; bind every receipt to input/candidate/checker/content population and enforce explicit success criteria.

findings.title: Postmerge content comparison collapses missing keys and null expected values.
findings.assessment: The expected loop compares observed.get(path) with expected_oid. Expected {a: None} versus observed {} yields no mismatch, and the reverse extra-path loop is empty. The independent finite model confirms equality on all 81 pairs of two-path string maps but exhibits this admitted-runtime counterexample outside the annotation.
findings.limits: String-valued maps preserve the intended finite relation; this is a missing runtime admission check, not a counterexample within that mathematical domain. No actual landed tree was observed.
findings.next_action: Require canonical nonempty digest strings and explicit key membership; preserve exact whole-map equality and immutable stored observations.

findings.title: Declared repository-relative paths and producer routes are not confinement boundaries.
findings.assessment: RepoPath accepts drive-colon, leading-backslash and NUL forms after normalization. canonical_repo_path silently erases leading slash and excess parent components, and path_is_under mishandles the POSIX root prefix. Producer routing interpolates an unvalidated filename. Actual canonicalize_path is filesystem/platform-dependent with a fallback, so it cannot be substituted for a purely lexical proof or atomic effect confinement.
findings.limits: No real path escaped or filesystem write occurred. The POSIX root observation is a portability gap; this checkout is Windows. Path-prefix guards can remain useful under explicit canonical base and no-race assumptions.
findings.next_action: Separate syntax admission, canonical relative identity, and checked effect-root confinement; reject absolute/drive/parent/control forms before normalization and bind file operations to the admitted root.

findings.title: Byte ceilings do not bound empty-message work or guarantee stream termination.
findings.assessment: Both streaming ingress loops make refusal depend on accumulated bytes. Arbitrarily many empty chunks/messages leave that measure unchanged. A finite control consumes 10001 messages at a one-byte ceiling. The statement that an endless stream is abandoned needs a byte-progress assumption or an independent step/deadline bound.
findings.limits: Memory/hash-prefix ceilings remain meaningful. No infinite stream was run; externally supplied receive/iterator latency and cleanup are also outside the byte proof.
findings.next_action: Add independently enforced message/iteration/deadline/cancellation budgets and preserve a receipt that distinguishes byte overflow from no-progress refusal.

findings.title: CAS license checks are local predicates, with missing finite-time admission.
findings.assessment: NaN expiry passes the >= expiration check. Validation checks expected-head equality and expiry only; it neither authenticates/rederives the license ID nor checks candidate identity, not-before, single-use or an atomic Git compare-and-swap. A randomized default nonce is a real current improvement but does not supply those authority properties.
findings.limits: No token generator, Git command or mutex was executed. A trusted caller may supply missing premises; this owner alone is not a reusable execution capability. The in-memory mutex does not establish prior worker fencing after recovery.
findings.next_action: Admit finite time values, bind all license semantics, and enforce issue/revocation/one-use/current-head checks atomically at the actual effect boundary.

findings.title: Identity construction permits evidence before execution despite the builder invariant.
findings.assessment: with_evidence rejects an uncreated execution slot. The constructor independently accepts either a reference or NotYetCreated for execution and evidence, and the parser delegates to that constructor, leaving the evidence-created/execution-uncreated combination admitted. This is an entry-point invariant mismatch within an otherwise strict closed codec.
findings.limits: The control abstracts correctly typed domain/slot references into created/uncreated Booleans. No forged signature or actual execution was claimed.
findings.next_action: Enforce the cross-slot invariant in the common constructor/parser boundary, then retain the same guard in transition helpers.

findings.title: WorkPacket mapping validation is weaker than a closed work-scope contract.
findings.assessment: The mapping path accepts empty individual path strings, overlapping write/forbidden declarations, arbitrary nonempty base labels and ignored schema/unknown keys. Direct WorkPacket construction validates only exact class and authority effect, bypassing even required-label and nonempty-write checks. This is a shape adapter unless stronger preconditions are explicit.
findings.limits: No actual work was scheduled. WorkPacket correctly canonicalizes authority enum by identity, unlike two other label objects; this finding does not claim authority escalation.
findings.next_action: Use one closed constructor for both entry points, validate schema/digests/canonical unique paths and cross-field scope exclusions, then bind the packet to the admission policy.

findings.title: Frozen wrappers and copied mapping proxies do not deeply freeze evidence.

Postmerge witnesses and reconciled results similarly retain mutable dictionaries. Self-hash revalidation can detect some later mutation, but unconditionally trusting a frozen record or stale ID cannot.

findings.title: Path leases can overwrite active scope or skip conflict checks by caller-selected stacking.
findings.assessment: A disjoint regrant under the same packet ID replaces the stored prior scope. stacked_under skips every overlap/resource check against the named lease without proving a relationship. The table has no expiry, fencing or concurrency control.

findings.title: Git hygiene admits broad staging through a pathspec delimiter.
findings.assessment: The policy refuses broad options before -- but accepts any nonempty path list after it, including git add -- . . Attached -Cfoo is not consumed as a global option and can bypass recognition of a protected subcommand. The policy is a token heuristic rather than a complete Git command admission grammar.
findings.limits: No Git commands executed. The direct argv witness is independent of shell parsing; broader shell wrapping remains outside this helper.

findings.title: Ownership-first reconciliation needs an explicit authoritative premise.
findings.assessment: Owned paths select the branch even when only main changed; foreign-owned paths select main even when only branch changed. Only unowned paths use ordinary three-way equality rules. Therefore fail-closed concurrent-edit language is conditional on ownership-map authority, not a general preservation property.
findings.limits: This can be intentional policy rather than a defect when exclusive ownership is authoritative and current. The control does not execute Git or claim any actual edit was lost.
findings.next_action: State and verify ownership freshness/exclusivity, bind the map into the candidate, and distinguish policy-selected discard from conflict-free content preservation.

The chaos STRICT scenario rejects only NOT_MEASURED, while the general STRICT checker rejects every non-MEASURED value. These helpers are not interchangeable authoritative census/measurement gates.

These are local representation/totality gaps, not additional cryptographic or execution authority.

A benign allowed token can therefore hide a separate disallowed local path on the same line. The four regex profiles also deliberately cover only selected path spellings.
findings.limits: This is a profile-scoped lexical detector, not a complete portability theorem. No original scanner or generated document pipeline executed.

The included free stake never carries a demand,as the earlier theorem and Python definition state,so it witnesses the no-index disjunct under every responder history preserving that stake. As written this prediction cannot discriminate delayed-demand behavior from the trivial free case; preserve it historically and exclude free/no-demand alternatives when designing a new discriminating task.

findings.title: Public Pair construction bypasses imposition carrier validation
findings.assessment: Pair exposes public i and j fields, while impose checks only j against the carrier size. On a one-datum regime, Pair {i:999,j:0} passes this check and is retained; satisfies subsequently indexes profiles[999]. A diagonal pair also bypasses Pair::new. This is a source-derived counterexample to arbitrary public-input safety, not a failure of the sorted pairs generated by internal enumeration. Validate both endpoints and distinctness at the admission boundary before workflow reuse.

findings.title: Automorphism budget count can overflow before refusal
findings.assessment: Automorphism perm_count uses ordinary u64 multiplication while canonicalization uses saturating multiplication. On a structureless21-datum carrier,21! exceeds u64::MAX, so overflow-checked execution panics rather than returning IsoBudgetError. On sufficiently large unchecked products factorial can wrap to0, bypassing the intended budget guard before factorial allocation. Wrapper data limits32 do not exclude the checked21-datum case. This is arithmetic/source analysis, not native execution.

findings.title: Surd radicand multiplication can wrap to a wrong exact result
findings.assessment: Surd::sqrt multiplies reduced rational numerator p by denominator d with ordinary i128 multiplication before squarefree decomposition. Let p=2^126+1 and d=4 (coprime, both representable). The mathematical product is2^128+4; unchecked release multiplication wraps to4, yielding sqrt(p/d)=1/2 instead of its large positive value. In overflow-checked mode this panics. Surd::mul similarly uses unchecked radicand multiplication. This contradicts the blanket exact-with-checked-overflow characterization outside the tiny fixtures; no Rust executable was run.

findings.title: Invariant fixed-label classifier is narrower than all equivariant observation
findings.assessment: symmetric_no_equivariant_classifier proves f(not x)=f(x) implies f(false)=f(true): invariance into a codomain with trivial action. The surrounding comment promotes this to no definable observer and says any observer requires orientation breaking. With Bool.not acting on BOTH domain and codomain, f=id is equivariant (f(not x)=not(f(x))) and separates false/true. The theorem is valid; the unqualified observer/equivariance interpretation exceeds its hypothesis. State fixed output labels/trivial codomain action, and distinguish abstract equivariant information from a chosen label.

findings.title: Two legacy double-boundary spot-checks query the wrong dimension
findings.assessment: The first two conjuncts of d2_zero_dims_2_3_4 query facets of a cell after two boundary operations. Their target lengths are n-1, while every resulting term has length n-2, so these zeros are automatic and do not test cancellation. For triangle(0,1,2), even the signless double boundary passes all queried edge checks although each correct vertex coefficient is2; the tetrahedron case has the analogous triangle-versus-edge mismatch. The third dimension4 conjunct queries two successive facets correctly. BoundaryCancellation independently proves every target coefficient zero and supplies correct signless counterexamples, so the stronger signed theorem is not undermined. Retain historical bytes but do not count the first two conjuncts as substantive cancellation tests.

Replace the open converse with an appropriately unoriented or closure-aware characterization; preserve historical bytes.

findings.statement: The appendix claims sigma=(-1)^(Nplus-Nminus) changes from negative to positive when the counts swap. The SU2 subsection repeats the unsupported implication. This is a direct algebraic contradiction in TeX and PDF, irrespective of receipt status.
findings.recommended_action: Retain as a negative control; withdraw the cancellation/physical sign claim until an actually sign-reversing, weight-preserving involution is specified and checked. Do not repair historical receipts to mask the contradiction.

findings.statement: PFP013 renderer extracts bold Author/Date/Version fields, but current paper.md uses centered plain header lines; rerunning that local tool would fall back to 2026-10-05 v0.1.0 metadata. No actual rendering or source overwrite was performed.

The teaching mutation helper accepts zero-length insertion strictly inside a protected span because its overlap test requires positive intersection length. Inserting X at2 in abcdef with protected[0,4) yields abXcdef. This violates preservation of the protected text; the production forge is a separate owner.
The teaching Inheritance DAG is an unchecked dictionary: a self-loop is accepted. The two-dictionary separation example is useful, but does not verify DAG acyclicity or causal descent.

The exact dominance helper silently zips unequal coordinate vectors, so(1,) dominates(0,100) on the truncated prefix. It correctly handles all81 tested equal-length rational pairs but implements neither dimension admission nor a population Pareto front.

The largest-remainder notebook converts exact quotas to floats before floor/ranking. At sufficiently large integer caps the resulting population can exceed the cap or indexing can fail; the recorded fixed36-case control retains concrete examples. Its cap20 example does not expose this precision limit.

Several headings promise mechanisms absent from the code: occurrence independence has no occurrence object, inverse PageRank is one damped sum, event replay is a payload/digest equality assertion, and homologous crossover is a list migration. Preserve these as explicitly limited teaching examples, not completed workflows or mathematical certificates.

The island migration helper removes the source genome before indexing the target. A nonexistent target raises IndexError after losing the genome from the source population. The notebook provides no atomicity/rollback boundary.

findings.claim: Exact native adapter coerces string false to True for positive-definite, boundary-closed and closure predicates; rank 1.9 becomes 1, and string success=false is truthy. Plain-text representation fails round-trip equality for valid TurnView names containing equals/colon, embedded newlines and surrounding whitespace. It also parses empty text as zero metrics. Exact information equivalence needs a stricter admitted syntax or escaping.
Glyph JSON parsing int-coerces a Boolean round and fractional metric before strict TurnView validation, accepting true as 1 and 1.9 as 1.

OESOS receipt is mutable, accepts an unverified broken chain and excludes metadata from its digest. Distinct metadata can share a receipt digest, and event mutation leaves a stale digest. Hashing selected fields is not immutable authenticated evidence.

findings.claim: Atom-count budget does not bound structural quantifier evaluation;64 outer branches with empty inner domain PASS at budget0 and make65 evaluator calls.
The composed-bound policy refuses a valid weaker upper bound: actual error1 and proven step bound1 imply bound2, but <=sum check returns R033_BOUND_NOT_COMPOSED.

Reachable-final plus no deadlock does not guarantee termination or a route to final from every reachable state. A separate closed live trap branch PASSes. This is a limit of the explicit predicate, not a contradiction of its existential-end clause.
No unit normalization is enforced for blind joint weights: row2 on a1x1 carrier passes with every table totaling4. Probability-language use needs an explicit normalized-input assumption.
Closed surface input claim is not enforced. Two tetrahedral sphere boundaries sharing one vertex pass all edge-incidence/angle/action checks despite a disconnected vertex link.
Universal edge-derived closure statement fails for allowed ordering/connectors. An actual S3 edge assignment with correctly recomputed faces refuses solely on nonidentity closure.
Derived record digests bind only id/value, not operation or input lineage; independent sum/product derivations share a digest. Historical immutability requires an external root/custody policy.
Principal self-handoff narrowing is ignored, unlike the general last-handoff prose. A read-only self-handoff followed by write task passes.
Unmapped target relation can silently alias a source relation via rename fallback. A typed mapR->S does not bind target-onlyR, yet equivalence passes by evaluating sourceR.
An initially empty-clause CNF cannot carry the natural zero-step refutation: checker refuses it as flag-without-proof. This is certificate incompleteness rather than unsound acceptance.
Chebyshev inequality is sufficient, not necessary for actual coverage; always-full[0,1] interval at n1,h1 is refused for alpha1/10 despite coverage1.
An explicitly OPEN claim disappears from frontier once any declared test link exists, even though test adequacy/results are not checked.
Missing fence-audit fields default clean even with a declared violation; no host audit recomputation occurs. Packet still cannot promote from permanent quarantine.
Malformed assertion_flags=null raises AttributeError outside typed refusal handling.
Exported encoder accepts NaN and is deterministic Python JSON, not strict RFC8785 canonical JSON as claimed.
Self-contained count/head header can be rewritten with a shortened valid prefix and new id; chain verifies without external head binding.
Unsafe-id hashed filename aliases the literal safe hex-digest id, and load does not bind requested id to header id.
Controller accepts a replay-valid CEC extension whose packet parent differs from the controller problem argument. It never binds the candidate packet to that requested problem.

findings.title: Legacy challenge scoring sends expected answers to the solver
findings.statement: cmd_challenge_score serializes the complete case, including expected/answer, as a solver argument. A fake solver that merely echoes that value receives CORRECT. This defeats the intended hidden-case separation before checker quality matters.
findings.next_action: Pass only explicitly public inputs; keep expected values solely in the host oracle and test adversarial echoing.
findings.limitations: Synthetic cases only; no actual hidden case, private key, executable deliverable or subprocess was accessed/executed.

findings.title: Challenge judge and freeze hashes are not recomputed at scoring
findings.statement: The scorer checks shared challenge IDs, equality of copied commitment strings and deliverable bytes, but never recomputes the judge commitment or freeze_record_hash. Mutating the synthetic expected answer while leaving both commitments unchanged still scores successfully.
findings.next_action: Recompute canonical commitments over the exact judge/task/limits and freeze payload; bind checker identity/source and reject any mismatch before dispatch.
findings.limitations: This is the legacy CLI scorer, not a claim about the separate accounted challenge adapter. Arbitrary hash strings were synthetic.

findings.title: The advertised dual checkers are one equality predicate duplicated
findings.statement: Both chk_a and chk_b evaluate expected == actual. They share all mistakes and cannot disagree except for a synthetic fault branch; Python also treats True equal to1. The control returns CORRECT for expected1 and answertrue.
findings.next_action: Use independent admitted predicates or accurately label one check; require exact JSON types before equality and bind the actual candidate field.
findings.limitations: Does not prove every task needs two implementations; it disproves the current independence claim and strict integer discrimination.

findings.title: Empty swarm verification emits Verified
findings.statement: The contract loader requires only the version. Empty verifier_routes return all_passed=True; absent targets produce no blocking audit, and cmd_run_swarm emits PASS_TO_MASTER/Verified. The complete orchestration control reproduced that outcome with fake I/O.
findings.next_action: Require nonempty bound verifier coverage and candidate targets, or classify the empty result as NOT_RUN/UNVERIFIED; bind each result to exact contract/candidate bytes.
findings.limitations: Governance precondition and all file/output operations were faked in the control; no original contract, command or corpus was modified.

findings.title: Task operations and budgets are declarations without execution isolation
findings.statement: Generic task allowed_operations/stopping_bounds are appended to objective prose. Swarm verifier commands run as subprocesses under repository cwd; allowed paths and budget fields are not an OS/tool/network/money boundary in this caller. A governance digest does not supply missing enforcement.
findings.next_action: Define which layer enforces each constraint and reject unsupported enforcement requests; report prompt-only limits as declarations and run untrusted commands only through an enforcing port.
findings.limitations: Static caller review; no command escape or network action was attempted. External launch/sandbox policy could add restrictions, but is not established by these functions.

findings.title: StageB can erase uncertain charges or accept invalid cost arithmetic
findings.statement: One reservation covers dispatch retries, which retain only the last response. Timeout/URL/OSError settles zero and releases the hold; usage fields are int-coerced, accepting negative/Boolean values and empty usage as zero. Budget.settle permits spend above its cap. Four isolated controls reproduce timeout release, negative/empty usage and over-cap settlement.
findings.next_action: Reserve and record each attempt; retain holds on unknown liability; validate exact nonnegative usage and billed amounts; stop with an accounting failure when actual liability exceeds the admitted cap.
findings.limitations: The stored1600-call sample has coherent nonnegative declared charges; this finding concerns failure behavior of the source runner if its lock/preflight admits a run. No paid call occurred.

findings.title: StageB raw custody is written after scoring and all parallel jobs
findings.statement: _one_call invokes score before creating the raw receipt, and run materializes every future before writing either JSONL file. An exception in scoring or one worker can prevent preservation of already completed, potentially billed responses. The known local detector NameError is one concrete scoring failure.
findings.next_action: Persist request/attempt/raw response before scoring, use per-attempt durable settlement/failure receipts, and collate worker failures without discarding completed evidence.
findings.limitations: Source-confirmed failure path, not a new provider experiment or proof that the historical saved run lost bytes. Canonical two-attempt ports have different behavior.

findings.title: Missing ladder observations become favorable empirical evidence
findings.statement: evaluate_hypotheses substitutes default accuracy, cost, heldout gain, bluff rates and zero error counts when evidence_data is absent or partial. These literals are passed into H1-H13 evaluation as if observed. Repeating the same P0 gate is replay agreement, not independent checking.
findings.next_action: Require complete provenance-bearing observations per hypothesis and return NOT_RUN/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when absent; put synthetic examples behind an explicit fixture-only mode.
findings.limitations: No domain hypothesis implementation or model was rerun. The defect is the caller manufacturing measurement inputs, regardless of each downstream acceptance threshold.

findings.title: Local detector crashes on the obstruction branch
findings.statement: run_local defines vertices, edges, omega and owner, then iterates undefined core when the delegated verdict is an obstruction. The synthetic obstruction control raises NameError instead of returning a red witness or refusal.
findings.next_action: Use the intended bound cochain and add red-branch witness/ownership controls; retain scoring failures without losing raw call custody.

EvaluateLlmTurnUseCase catches parsing exceptions, but required-field membership and parsed.get run afterward; a valid JSON number/list/null can raise instead of producing a typed refusal. findings.title: An opaque dual reference is treated as enough for exact reply structure
findings.statement: The legacy turn evaluator only checks dual_witness_ref truthiness when residual_colour is Exact. Its inherited-meaning detector checks two prose phrases. Those checks cannot establish witness feasibility, candidate/problem binding or semantic validity; ACCEPTED must remain structural only.

findings.statement: build_payload_from_prompt_artifact carries required_reply_fields and body identity but does not pass artifact.kill_conditions into LlmTurnPayloadV1.create. Downstream policy can therefore differ from the compiled artifact despite the shared artifact ID.

findings.title: Stage7 replay return is bound to labels rather than witness bodies
findings.statement: The caller validates replay type/demo/stage/count/candidate_id/expected_accept but does not compare a digest of each submitted witness or problem. Reusing matching labels can conceal a stale result unless the injected verifier enforces full binding itself.

findings.title: Pilot-suite objective digest omits grading and resource inputs
findings.statement: The objective hash includes pilot/model/checker label and messages, but omits the expected answer, source hashes and call/token/cost limits used by the run. Different grading/resource contracts can therefore share the same objective identity.

findings.limitations: Run ID and stored summaries provide additional identity; no claim that they are overwritten or that concrete accounting adapters ignore their own plan. This is an incomplete objective commitment.

findings.title: Corpus freezing hashes ambiguous IDs rather than content
findings.statement: Joining sorted IDs with commas collides for ["a,b","c"] and ["a","b,c"]. No sample content is bound. The isolated helper control produces identical digests for these different synthetic sample sets.
findings.next_action: Use length-delimited/canonical structured IDs plus per-sample content digests, and bind empirical counts to exact sample membership/receipts.

findings.title: Coboundary score schema permits undefined rationals and inconsistent flags
findings.statement: The rational regex admits 1/0 and00/00, and the schema accepts is_exact_candidate=true with is_legal=false when its other syntactic conditions are met. The schema-only control validates such a record.

findings.title: Finite CSP normalization silently changes the supplied mathematical state
findings.statement: normalize_state applies str to variable names and int to values before checking duplicates. The control maps x=1.9,y=true to integer x=1,y=1, so malformed/noninteger inputs are solved as a different state.

findings.statement: from_wire advertises canonical parsing but accepts whitespace, leading zeros, denominator-one and nonreduced fractions, negative denominator, plus sign and negative zero. Feasible primal/dual witnesses and the same constrained problem are absent. An inconsistent(1,0,0,True) record is accepted. Equal values can be an arithmetic gap result only; optimality requires separately validated feasibility and weak duality. No concrete workflow accepting this record has yet been found.

Its byte-preservation guarantee survives this counterexample; interpreting the receipt as preserving role semantics does not.

findings.statement: A nested App f(App g(Atom x)) renders (f (g x)) but the parser makes two atom arguments, so parse(serialize(term)) differs from term for an admitted recursive model.
