findings.title: Proofreading admits arithmetic-looking pseudo-prose without a mathematical check
findings.statement: The HopfieldNinioProofreader describes preventing pseudo-proofs and surviving orthogonal deformation, but its actual predicate is marker/buzzword detection plus caller-supplied residual. findings.title: DDC step-chain hashes omit metrics and timestamps.
findings.assessment: The step hash input contains class/carrier/witness/receipt labels but excludes phi_1, gamma_2 and timestamp. Two admitted steps with identical included fields and different metrics therefore have the same prehash input and head while producing different metric histories. State hashes also hash class labels rather than state bytes.
findings.limits: An omitted-field projection, not a SHA collision or a demonstrated historical tampering event. A separate immutable full receipt may supply the missing binding, but this head alone does not.
findings.next_action: Before using the tape head to bind evaluator results, hash the complete canonical step including metrics and time/policy semantics or explicitly bind a separately checked full-step digest.

findings.title: Compensation heads bind branch ID and count rather than branch contents.
findings.assessment: record_compensation_branch checks authority and nonempty class labels, but the hash record includes only branch_id and step_count alongside chain metadata. Different branch tapes of the same length can share a head in separate histories; branch DFA validity is not checked here.
findings.limits: Duplicate IDs within one evaluator are refused. The finite counterexample concerns two histories and does not claim a hash collision.
findings.next_action: Bind the complete ordered compensation steps and run the intended dialect/adjacency checks before treating a compensation head as evidence of the branch.

findings.title: OEARS terminal refusal conflicts with complete-tape admission.
findings.assessment: The OEARS M rule permits no following token, while complete validation requires the final token T for every dialect. M is a valid refusal prefix, M is incomplete, and M T is rejected. Thus no completed OEARS tape can contain that terminal refusal.
findings.limits: Exact contradiction in the inspected rules; no Rust execution. Legacy M T semantics differ and are not covered by this counterexample.
findings.next_action: Choose one explicit OEARS completion rule for refusal and align complete validation, terminalized state, replay and tests with it.

findings.title: Exact per-step metrics do not guarantee exact bounded window arithmetic.
findings.assessment: Metrics are reduced to Rational64 individually, then sliding-window sum/mean uses unchecked Rational64 additions. Two individually representable i64-max integer metrics already require an unrepresentable sum. Missing metrics also enter history as zero, which conflates unavailable and measured zero for these summaries.
findings.limits: Exact arithmetic representability control only. Compiled dependency overflow behavior was not run; the report does not choose panic or wrap as the observed result.
findings.next_action: Use arbitrary-precision accumulation or checked arithmetic with an explicit refusal, and retain unavailable metrics as unavailable.

findings.title: Scheduler status and completion are not enforced task outcomes.
findings.assessment: SceneSpec validates allowed_result_statuses, but scheduler.advance checks scene identity without checking membership in that set or assigned producer identity. A terminal scene becomes COMPLETED for any non-stop status: with allowed PASS and empty stop list, an incoming HOLD becomes COMPLETED. Continuation halt similarly marks any nonempty history COMPLETED. complete_bout uses a fixed PASS/changed_state=1 completion input for traversal.
findings.limits: These are choreography labels; they may intentionally mean run termination. They must not be consumed as accepted-task evidence. Stronger receipt bindings elsewhere do not change this transition predicate.
findings.next_action: Enforce declared scene/producer admission and separate terminated, halted, exhausted and task-accepted states in executable experiment accounting.

findings.title: Residual worsening can reset the no-progress counter.
findings.assessment: run_swarm sets refined_residual=1 whenever post_residual differs from pre_residual. For residual1 to2, delta is positive and status HOLD, but progressed is true and scheduler dry_rounds resets. The oscillation detector also receives that positive progress signal.
findings.limits: Total step/unit and visit bounds remain; this is a stagnation semantics defect rather than an infinite-loop claim.
findings.next_action: Define progress against a task-preserving ordered residual or a separately checked refinement relation; record mere change independently.

findings.title: PASS_TO_MASTER publication checks verdict without binding the current task/candidate.
findings.assessment: skill_run parses a checker receipt and requires Accepted for PASS_TO_MASTER, but does not compare its candidate content digest/optional candidate ID with the current task, objective or selected candidate. The checker parser itself supplies those identity fields; publication retains them without establishing the relationship.
findings.limits: No forged receipt or filesystem publication was executed. This is the standalone writer boundary; a correctly binding caller can supply the missing assurance.
findings.next_action: Require an exact task/candidate/checker-policy binding and successful task-specific receipt validation before publishing an accepted answer.

findings.title: Nested dialectic budgets are local copies, not a conserved experiment budget.
findings.assessment: AdversaryMachine.nest opens a child with the unchanged parent remaining budget. Two children of a100 budget can each spend60 under their local checks. This is valid local accounting but exceeds a shared100 experiment cap.
findings.limits: The separate active PFP gateway has reservation/recovery mechanisms (RAD-C02); this finding must not be generalized to that ledger. No provider spend occurred.
findings.next_action: Document local budget scope or reserve each child allocation from one shared controller before any live dispatch.

findings.title: Generic boundary trailers do not establish production qualification.
findings.assessment: Sixty-nine complete matching trailers instantiate the same bounded-count mechanism after nominal origin/claim/identifier substitutions. Their tests exercise count admission rather than the enclosing carrier, scheduler or provider algorithm. Other trailers construct Ok/Err directly. Mutation-accounting comments therefore cannot establish the claimed production mutation campaign from these bodies.
findings.limits: All distinct owner prefixes and every template residual were reviewed. This does not imply all meaningful tests elsewhere are absent; separately referenced test targets were not run or granted reading credit.
findings.next_action: Keep finite count tests as count tests. Qualify actual workflow predicates using bound negative controls and real task failures; do not use trailer counts as experiment success evidence.

findings.title: Response-schema numeric semantics need an explicit dialect contract.
findings.assessment: The local integer type admits values representable through as_i64/as_u64, and number equality compares rendered strings. Mathematical1 and1.0 can therefore differ, and larger exact integers are outside that integer predicate. Regex and local-ref handling are also a deliberately restricted implementation.
findings.limits: No external schema validator or serde runtime was invoked. This is a concrete language-boundary review, not a claim of whole-standard conformance failure.
findings.next_action: Freeze the supported numeric/ref/regex dialect for provider outputs and test equivalent numeric encodings against it; avoid presenting the subset as interchangeable with every schema evaluator.

findings.title: Carrier and matrix admission do not establish the intended topology automatically.
findings.assessment: Public Network::new checks edge endpoints but accepts faces without their boundary. The JSON parser is stronger. Separately, primary gates verify declared matrix algebra without reconstructing incidence matrices from the supplied carrier. Thus algebraic witness acceptance needs an explicit encoding relation to the intended complex/task.
findings.limits: The direct constructor witness does not bypass the stronger JSON parser. Valid declared matrices can support a correct finite theorem even when their application interpretation remains unproved.
findings.next_action: Centralize validated complex construction and bind/recompute oriented incidence matrices from that carrier before using cohomology or LP certificates as task evidence.

findings.statement: validate_pullback and validate_pushout omit their declared object/leg boundaries. In the lawful terminal category{A,id_A}, set every named morphism to id_A but all declared apex/left/right object fields to Ghost. The square commutes, and every searched Hom involving Ghost is empty, so the universal loop has no candidate cones and returns no violation. A nonexistent object is thus accepted as the proposed pullback/pushout. Canonical ambient-category validation alone cannot repair this missing diagram admission.

check_terminal and check_initial only iterate ambient objects; they never first require the proposed object to belong to the category. In the valid empty category both loops are vacuous and any label passes, although there is no terminal or initial object. This is a missing existence check distinct from the hom-set uniqueness condition.

check_local_confluence accepts a formal-inverse homotopy as a join when the forward branches have no common descendant. For a->b and a->c with b,c irreducible, declare paths r_ab;r_ab^-1 and r_ac;r_ac^-1 and a homotopy between them. Both paths run a->a and pass the structural validator; the checker then reports local confluence and termination despite the two distinct normal forms. This is a chosen zigzag/homotopy condition, not ordinary directed local confluence, and cannot be used with the usual terminating-plus-local-confluence conclusion.

A level2 RewriteCell inserted through add_higher_cell can connect nonparallel paths and still validate. check_two_cell_endpoints only checks that both paths exist; parallel boundary validation occurs only for the separate homotopies map, whose coverage/agreement with cells is not enforced. Paths a->b and c->d with distinct endpoints, joined by such a level2 cell and an empty homotopies map, pass every visible validator stage. The admitted data need not be globular even at level2.

ValidatedInfinityRewriteSystem exposes its sole declared field publicly, so callers can construct the wrapper directly or mutate it after validate. The type therefore cannot serve as an enduring admission token even for the limited reference/shape predicates its constructor checks. Other private validated owners in this audit avoid this specific bypass.

ValidatedFiniteTwoCategory::try_new returns Ok unconditionally, with a placeholder for full validation. A declaration containing object A and no1-identity is accepted; id_1(A) then reaches unreachable because the promised map is absent. No identity, composition, associativity, globularity or interchange admission occurs in this constructor. This is directly visible source behavior; independent branch control is not a Rust run.

lawvere.rs identifies a Lawvere theory as a Cauchy-complete monoid in Prof, but supplies no finite-power/product structure or product-preserving presentation. Idempotent completeness is insufficient: the one-object C2 group category has only the identity idempotent, which splits, yet no terminal object because its sole endomorphism set has two elements. The defining zero-fold product is therefore absent. The implementation should be treated as syntax and selected substitution checks, not that claimed characterization.

primary_source.title: F. William Lawvere, Functorial Semantics of Algebraic Theories, PNAS50(1963)
primary_source.consulted: The original definition requires objects to be finite powers of a distinguished object, including the zero-fold product. Only that definition/presentation passage is used; idempotent completeness alone is not that structure.

findings.statement: validate_splitting never reads the declared carrier or any morphism boundaries. Holding the three accepted equations and retract identity fixed while changing carrier from A to a nonexistent Ghost leaves validation successful and produces ValidatedIdempotentSplitting. The three equations are useful conditional checks but do not bind the claimed splitting to its carrier or an admitted category.

The older coend owner identifies diagonal elements with equal images in F(c,c-prime), instead of the two diagonal images of each element of F(c-prime,c). For C the walking arrow A->B and F=Hom_C, both identities map to f in Hom(A,B), so the source algorithm merges them. The true coend has two classes because Hom(B,A) is empty and the identity-arrow relations are trivial. The embedded coend_with_identification test expects precisely this incorrect merge. A lawful bifunctor therefore yields the wrong cardinality.

primary_source.title: Emily Riehl, Categorical Homotopy Theory
primary_source.consulted: The coend coequalizer has source coproduct indexed by arrows f of H(cod f,dom f), with both maps into diagonal contributions. Only this defining formula is used. The walking-arrow Hom counterexample is the audit own finite inference.

findings.statement: coend.compute writes union-find root IDs into class_of, but classes is the dense vector of classes_map values. After unions of A0 with B0 and then A1 with B0 in a diagonal inventory A0,A1,A2,B0, roots are1 and2 while classes has length2. A2 maps to2, which is outside the advertised class-index range. Root IDs must be remapped to dense class positions; equality-only dinaturality checks do not expose this mismatch.

FiniteReportPresheaf::new computes(1u64 << carrier_size)-1 before validate_contexts rejects carrier_size>64. Input65 therefore reaches an overflowing u64 shift before the advertised CarrierTooLarge refusal. With overflow checks enabled, including normal debug builds, this panics. This is a source-order and Rust-language inference, not a compiled reproduction; alternate compiler check settings are not assigned the same behavior.

primary_source.title: The Rust Reference: integer overflow
primary_source.consulted: Out-of-range integer subtraction and shifting by at least the left type bit width are overflow; debug-mode checks panic and compiler flags control checks. Used for source-visible subtraction and pre-validation u64 shift ordering, without running Rust.

findings.statement: classify_cover bounds only the final product of local report counts, then materializes Cartesian prefixes in cover order. A valid presheaf with counts empty:1,A:N,B:0,AunionB:0 has final product0 for cover[A,B], so limit0 passes, yet the first prefix allocates N tuples. Reversing the cover avoids this allocation. The numerical final-product test is correct but does not bound intermediate enumeration work; this is an operational limit gap, not a false sheaf-cover result.

TriangleWitness is described for monotone maps on a finite chain but never checks monotonicity. Taking both left and right maps to be the swap[1,0] gives both composites equal to identity, so both triangle equations and both unit/counit inequalities hold. The maps reverse0<1 and fail the Galois equivalence atx=0,y=0. Thus these predicates alone do not certify an adjunction of chain categories.

AgentFunctor.map_skill_morphism does not preserve the represented SkillMorphism composition: mapping f >> g gives Agent[f >> g], while composing Agent[f] with Agent[g] gives Agent[f] >> Agent[g]. There is no quotient or equality rule identifying those IDs. Separately, SkillMorphism.try_associate compares only four fields even though derived PartialEq includes descriptions, whose two bracketings differ. These are metadata operations with limited field checks, not validated categorical functor/associativity laws on full SkillMorphism values.

IntegerFiniteCategoryWitness admits the reflexive graph with objects0,1,2 and arrows(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(0,1),(1,2). Every endpoint is in range and every object has a loop, so its complete visible predicate passes. The composable pair0->1->2 has no possible0->2 composite; no category with exactly that arrow inventory exists. Loop existence is not identity or composition certification.

ProductCardinality checks pair-tag syntax and vector length but not unique Cartesian membership. With declared sizes2 and2, four copies of a|x are admitted as four objects even though there is only one distinct pair. The witness therefore establishes a list-size equation, not a complete product-object inventory.

DiscreteCleavageWitness uses only source/target base-object labels when counting lifts, never the projected base arrow. For the valid functor from the terminal category into the one-object group C2, the sole total identity maps to the base identity, so the nonidentity base arrow has no lift. Encoding both base arrows as(0,0) and the sole total arrow as(0,0) passes the source count loop twice. Boundary multiplicity is not cartesian-lift evidence; category and functor admission are also absent.

primary_source.title: The Stacks Project, Definitions4.35.1 and4.38.2
primary_source.consulted: Definition4.35.1 requires a lift of each base morphism into each object above its target, together with a unique factorization condition. Definition4.38.2 adds discrete fibers to a category already fibred in groupoids; discrete fibers alone do not give that lifting property.

findings.statement: EnrichedCompositionDimWitness claims and requires dim(A,C)=dim(A,B)*dim(B,C). Enriched composition only needs a morphism from the tensor of the two hom objects into the third, not an isomorphism. The unital associative algebra F2 x F2 defines a valid one-object vector-space-enriched category: its hom-object has dimension2, while the composition domain has dimension4. The source guard rejects2,2,2. Its product arithmetic would be valid for tensor-domain dimension but not the documented target hom dimension.

primary_source.title: G. M. Kelly, Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory
primary_source.location: Section1.2, printed page8/PDF page14, definition and equations1.3-1.4
primary_source.consulted: The definition provides a composition morphism from the tensor of two hom objects into the third hom object, with associativity/unit equations. It does not require this morphism to be invertible. Only this definition passage was used.

limits: Independent exact four-element algebra countermodel and the defining enriched-composition axiom; no original Rust execution.

findings.statement: ChainComplexCategory::degree_span accepts ordered i32 endpoints but subtracts them in i32 before casting. Bounds i32::MIN and i32::MAX pass validate_shell yet their span4294967295 exceeds i32::MAX. With overflow checks enabled, including normal debug builds, the accessor panics instead of returning its representable u32 span. This is a source-level arithmetic/profile inference; no Rust build was run.

primary_source.title: The Rust Reference: integer overflow
primary_source.consulted: Out-of-range integer subtraction and shifting by at least the left type bit width are overflow; debug-mode checks panic and compiler flags control checks. Used for source-visible subtraction and pre-validation u64 shift ordering, without running Rust.

findings.statement: CoproductIndex::try_new always encodes the first right-summand element to run a sample round trip. If right=0 this nonexistent element triggers OutOfRange, so even the valid finite coproduct1+0 is refused;0+1 succeeds. This hidden asymmetric domain restriction is absent from the cardinal-sum contract. The separate CoproductCardinalities owner correctly permits zero inputs.

GroupCocycle is documented as a normalized integer2-cochain cocycle check, but it reduces the coboundary modulo n and never checks normalization. At n=3 the normalized row-major table[0,0,0,0,1,0,0,0,2] passes every residue test while its integer coboundary at(1,1,2) equals-3. At n=2 the constant-one table passes but is not normalized. The implementation is meaningful for unnormalized trivial-action Z/n-valued cocycles, not the documented integer/normalized carrier.

primary_source.title: Brian Conrad, Group Cohomology handout
primary_source.consulted: Cocycles have zero coboundary in the specified coefficient module; the bar differential gives the degree-two formula used in the independent finite control. Only these definition passages are used.

limits: Independent exact finite countermodels, not original Rust execution. The coefficient distinction follows by applying the referenced differential definition to the implemented arithmetic.

findings.statement: MonadKleisliCensus rejects equal unit and multiplication reference strings. For the identity monad T=Id, both transformations are legitimately Id=>Id and may be the very same identity transformation. The singleton identity monad satisfies every law and has one Kleisli identity/hom, but the equal-label guard refuses it. Different names are not a mathematical condition for identity injection.

StateCardinalityWitness computes |A|*|S| while its comment calls this StateT cardinality. For the ordinary identity-base, total finite-set state construction S->(A x S), cardinality is (|A|*|S|)^|S|: with two values and two states,16 computations versus the reported4 output pairs. The multiplication is correct for pair cardinality, not the stated state-transformer carrier.

primary_source.title: transformers-0.6.2.0, Control.Monad.Trans.State.Strict
primary_source.consulted: Official package API defines StateT by a function from state to an inner-monad result/state pair; State specializes the inner monad to Identity. Only these definitions were used.

limits: Finite total-function interpretation with identity inner monad; no Haskell bottoms, partiality or arbitrary effect cardinalities are being counted.

findings.statement: CoreflectorCount assigns counits=subcategory_objects, but the counit of inclusion i:A->C left adjoint to coreflector c:C->A is i*c=>Id_C and is indexed by ambient objects. For C the chain0<1 and A={0}, the genuine coreflection has counit components0->0 and0->1; try_new(2,1) reports one. Its integer guard supports a subcategory count, not the full counit-family count suggested by the type/accessor.

ValidatedFiniteMonad does not validate its declared category. On the nonassociative three-element unital magma from RCT-P01, the identity endomap and eta=mu=e satisfy its functor, boundary, naturality and monad-equation predicates. The host structure is not a category, so category admission is a necessary missing premise despite the private monad wrapper.

Generic EMAlgebra::verify_laws calls two methods that unconditionally return true; AlgebraMorphism::respects_algebras also returns true without invoking its comparison closure. For Maybe<bool>, the constant-false action violates the unit law at true but is accepted by this visible generic branch. The separate four-shell bool checker uses a different, lawful fixed action and does not justify the generic APIs.

The legacy adjunction validator checks triangle identities without unit/counit naturality. On the valid one-object S3 category with both functors identity, a noncentral transposition as both unit and counit satisfies both triangles but fails naturality against a second transposition. It can also skip triangles when present component names have no functor image. Thus its passing report does not certify an adjunction.

Legacy adjunction validation overwrites cloned embedded functor maps from independent public legacy maps, but DerivedMonad reads the embedded maps and DerivedComonad mixes both representations. Starting from a valid singleton identity adjunction, clearing only embedded left maps leaves the validated legacy data unchanged yet derives an empty monad object/arrow/multiplication map. Its law helpers then return no violations by empty iteration. No immutable validated wrapper connects these steps.

The hom-adjunction validator establishes bijections only for supplied pairs, with no complete pair coverage or naturality. An empty witness vector passes vacuously. Even with the sole pair fully covered, inversion on the C3 hom-set is an exact bijection but fails naturality for identity functors: inverse(0+1)=2 differs from inverse(0)+1=1. Therefore its finite round-trip check is not a full hom-adjunction certificate.

ValidatedFiniteNatTrans does not admit its functor arguments. For a valid singleton category with identity e, two declared identity object maps with empty arrow maps and component e pass all visible natural-transformation checks: the naturality loop skips each missing F(e) or G(e). Neither declaration is a total functor. Independent functor validation would reject both.

ValidatedFiniteOperad::try_new omits associativity. A one-color, three-unary-operation table with unit e, a*a=b and a*b=b*a=b*b=e satisfies every constructor check, yet (a*a)*b=e differs from a*(a*b)=a. This is source-checked admission of a nonassociative structure, not a native Rust replay.

The same constructor checks only declared composition entries and never requires each operation color to belong to colors. An empty declared color set with unary X->X operation e, identity X:e and e∘e=e passes its visible loops; partial substitution tables containing only units also pass. Thus even the declared carrier and full composition domain are not certified.
limits: Direct branch analysis; no claim of runtime execution or exhaustive malformed-data coverage.

findings.statement: CumulativeHLevelWitness reverses truncation-level cumulativity: it accepts observed GROUPOID=1 for claimed SET=0 and rejects observed SET=0 for claimed GROUPOID=1. Under the stated semantics, an observed n-type supports claims at larger levels, not smaller ones. The two unit tests explicitly expect the reversed outcomes.

primary_source.title: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics, first-edition-611-ga1a258c
primary_source.consulted: Official book theorem and proof passage: an n-type is also an(n+1)-type. Only this direction/hierarchy fact is used; no claim to have read the whole book.

limits: The check has no actual homotopy-type carrier or witness; correcting the inequality alone would not establish such a witness.

findings.statement: The legacy check_identity_law helper invents identity names id_<object> instead of receiving actual category identities. The valid unique functor from singleton(A,e) to singleton(X,i), mapping e to i, fails this helper because id_A is absent. This naming defect is confined to the legacy helper; the aggregate functor owner uses actual identity maps, with separate category-admission/composition gaps recorded below.

InitialArrowFamily compares aggregate arrows and targets, not each hom-set cardinality. In the valid two-object category C2 disjoint-union point, Hom(A,A) has2 arrows and Hom(A,B) has0; total outgoing arrows=objects=2 passes the numeric guard although A is not initial. IdentityLaw likewise assigns identities=objects from arrows>=objects without identifying concrete identities. These wrappers establish count predicates only.

ValidatedFiniteFunctor accepts declared source/target categories without invoking their validator. The identity mapping of an object-only structure with no arrows or identities passes all five functor checks because missing category identities and absent compositions are skipped. The separate finite-category validator correctly refuses that structure; its admission is not automatically inherited.

compose_validated_functors checks middle-category names rather than exact data. Identity maps into a C2 middle and out of a differently structured two-element idempotent middle, both named D, pass the name gate; their returned identity-map composite fails a*a preservation. The output is a raw DeclaredFiniteFunctor, so a separate revalidation catches the defect, but the documented exact-middle requirement is unenforced.

findings.title: ZeroCollision replay can accept an outcome when the decision refuses the quotient.
findings.assessment: The collision branch checks only known metric pair, zero distance and inequivalence. It omits carrier equality and E⊆Z. In the admitted three-point pseudometric d01=0,d02=d12=1 with E={{0,2},{1}}, decide_separation refuses IdentificationNotZero, while replay accepts collision(0,1). The enum explicitly says the outcome assumes E⊆Z, so the replay promise is false for this branch.
findings.next_action: Reapply input carrier/quotient admission in the collision branch, then validate the chosen zero witness without requiring a canonical pair.

findings.title: Opening totality claim contradicts rational constructor
findings.statement: rational.rs says every routine is total and none panics on caller data, but rq(n,0) explicitly panics and a should_panic test confirms that design. checked_ratio is the data-safe alternative.
findings.limits: Documentation inconsistency; panic is locally documented and not a failure of checked_ratio. No Rust execution.

findings.title: Binary field admission accepts reducible even moduli and degree zero
findings.statement: is_irreducible_binary tries only divisors with constant term1 and never requires positive degree. BinaryField::new(2,4) therefore admits modulus x²: encoded2 is nonzero but its square is0. new(0,1) admits an order-one carrier. The constructor claim that every admitted modulus is irreducible is false.
findings.limits: Independent mask model,127 polynomials degree<=6:23 false admissions including the constant1 case. Standard first-irreducible search starts odd and valid degrees1..4 retained sound bounded arithmetic checks. No source execution.

findings.title: Public field elements are not admitted to their carrier
findings.statement: FieldElement.coeffs is public; even a searched valid GF4 accepts [] beside [1,0], with add returning [] by zip and trace_value subsequently indexing an empty sum. Longer vectors can index past product. No length, coefficient range or field identity is checked.
findings.limits: Malformed/publicly assembled element boundary; generated canonical elements under valid small field assumptions avoid it. Raw FiniteField::new already documents a separate irreducibility trust premise.

findings.title: Binary operations disagree on out-of-carrier masks and raw phases
findings.statement: For valid GF4 modulus7, mul(4,1)=0 but mul(1,4)=3; arbitrary usize arguments are neither refused nor consistently reduced. Public BinaryPauli.phase allows values>3; adjoint uses 4-phase and mul adds raw u8 values, yielding debug overflow/panic or wrapped release arithmetic instead of typed refusal.
findings.limits: Canonical masks0..3 and phases0..3 avoid this counterexample. This is missing admission, not a failed law on valid field elements; no Rust panic executed.

findings.title: Subset builder silently assumes generator count equals field degree
findings.statement: build_line_group documents every subset but iterates 0..field.order. For degree1 and two generators it returns only masks0,1, omitting subsets2,3; fewer generators produce repeated rows. No commutation/independence check establishes a line group.
findings.limits: Expected Weyl-line callers may supply exactly degree independent commuting generators; this function does not enforce that contract. Large generator counts also risk unchecked shift width.

findings.title: Character-sum verifier can certify a vacuous nonfield
findings.statement: Unchecked FiniteField::new(0,1,[]) enumerates zero elements. Both nonzero-coefficient loops are empty, so verify_character_sum_identities returns field_order0 and zero checked counts without ever testing a field or sum equation. Public counts carry no modulus/scalar binding.
findings.limits: Caller violated the raw constructor field premise; searched constructor excludes it. This is a missing verifier admission gate, not false acceptance for an admitted genuine finite field.

findings.title: Quadratic Gauss-norm prose omits odd characteristic
findings.statement: The advertised norm-squared=q for every nonzero quadratic coefficient is false in characteristic2: in GF2, a1,b0 gives sum 1+(-1)=0, squared norm0, not2. The actual equality checker correctly refuses it.
findings.limits: Claim-scope issue only; source origin explicitly discusses odd-prime controls and does not bypass the equality check.

findings.title: Mutation-labeled tests do not call arithmetic owners
findings.statement: integer_factorization and residue inline mutation tests only construct literal Ok(1)/Err strings and assert variant labels. Their six-killed comments therefore do not furnish evidence for primality, factorization budgets, CRT correctness or negative mathematical controls.
findings.limits: Explicit sibling integration test targets may supply additional evidence outside this slice; not claiming all repository tests are vacuous.

findings.title: Gaussian norm realization needs reduced rational limbs
findings.statement: realize_norm tests numerator and denominator separately with two_squares without reducing the rational. BigRational::new_raw(3,3) represents1, whose Gaussian norm witness is1+0i, but the numerator3 immediately returns None. In the same module norm_class cancels the two odd3 valuations and propose_obstruction returns none. The negative realization verdict is therefore representation-dependent.
findings.limits: Requires an unreduced but nonzero-denominator positive Ratio spelling obtainable through public upstream new_raw; normalized Rational::new avoids it. No native dependency execution. Rational root owner already explicitly handles unreduced spellings; realization has no documented reduced-only input gate.

findings.title: Power-basis helper allocates before checked shape admission
findings.statement: invert_by_multiplication_matrix computes vec![zero;dim*dim] using unchecked usize multiplication before invoking BasicMatrix::from_row_major. At64bit dim=2^32, mathematical square is2^64: debug arithmetic panics, release multiplication wraps0 and subsequent nonempty column writes can index out of bounds. Return Option does not cover this input failure.
findings.limits: Direct public helper boundary. Fixed cyclotomic callers may pass tiny compile-time dimensions; no huge allocation, callback, backend or Rust execution performed.

findings.title: Public refinement does not establish root record properties
findings.statement: RootLocation::Isolated is documented as a unique irrational root, yet refine_simple_root(2x-1,[0,1],tolerance1) returns Isolated without bisection although its unique root1/2 is rational. With an untrusted interval, x^3-x over[-2,2] and tolerance4 passes the sole sign-change gate despite three roots. refine_root also copies a public Exact(123), multiplicity0 record unchanged for x²-2.
findings.limits: The rational-tag example satisfies the simple/isolating interval premise. The multi-root and foreign Exact examples deliberately violate documented caller trust assumptions; isolate_real_roots performs actual Sturm isolation and lattice recognition and is not shown unsound. Root records are not standalone verified certificates.

findings.title: Cyc24 cube-root exponent overflows before reduction
findings.statement: Cyc24::zeta3_pow(k:i32) promises any integer exponent but evaluates 8*k before zeta24 reduces modulo24. k=536870912 gives exact residue16 and wrapped i32 residue0, yielding a different field element with overflow checks disabled; checked builds panic.
findings.limits: Exact fixed-width independent model, not a Rust run. Ordinary small exponents and other fixed zeta constructors that reduce first are unaffected.

findings.title: Real embedding refinement limit is a working limit
findings.statement: The comment says MAX_REFINEMENTS guards only corrupt state, but valid irrational root enclosures at conductor8 with requested width W/2^400000 from current widthW require the final refinement before success. The last condition check is at399992bits, then the loop returns PrecisionLimit without rechecking. Arbitrary positive rational tolerance is otherwise admitted.
findings.limits: Typed refusal is safe; this contradicts the claimed corruption-only scope, not soundness of returned enclosures. Exact iteration-bound control avoids expensive native execution.

findings.title: Public real-root record can certify a foreign point sign
findings.statement: At conductor8, mutate the public CyclotomicRealRoot endpoints to a=b=-1, retaining polynomial x²-2. sign_of_poly(t) takes the equal-point branch and returns-1, whereas the intended canonical root sqrt2 is positive; it never replays root membership. Polynomial, Sturm chain and conductor are independently mutable.
findings.limits: Normal constructor correctly isolates the intended root. This is an untrusted-record/caller mutation boundary, distinct from the private RealEmbeddings and generic standard_real_sign paths.

findings.title: Unchecked ordered-field vectors lose terms in addition
findings.statement: FieldElementFPlus publicly exposes and directly deserializes conductor/coeffs. A conductor8 raw vector[0,0,1] represents theta²=2 through as_cyclotomic, but addition of zero reads only the two canonical positions and returns zero; short vectors panic at indexing. FieldElementF likewise has public nested conductors and derived unchecked deserialization.
findings.limits: Normal constructors reduce to the proper dimension. Countercontrol targets admitted public/Serde representation bypasses, not arithmetic on canonical constructor output.

findings.title: Polynomial enclosure lacks nonpositive tolerance refusal
findings.statement: CyclotomicRealRoot::bound_poly(theta,epsilon0) at the valid conductor8 initial interval computes Lipschitz bound1 and target0, then bisects forever: sqrt2 is never a rational midpoint, so width remains positive at every finite step. Negative epsilon also cannot terminate. Unlike refine_to_width, this public method has no positive-width gate.
findings.limits: Analytic loop-invariant counterexample plus128bounded exact bisections; no intentionally nonterminating program executed. Constant polynomials and conductor4 return early; positive tolerance with valid root state terminates mathematically.

findings.title: Zero-row GF2 matrix bypasses axis bound before augmentation overflow
findings.statement: F2Matrix::zeros(0,usize::MAX) passes checked rows*cols<=MAX_F2_ENTRIES and allocates no words. solve(empty_vector) then evaluates self.cols+1 unchecked in build_solve_augmented, panicking in checked-overflow builds before the promised typed TooLarge refusal. Nullspace also allocates directly from the unbounded column axis.
findings.limits: Own fixed-word arithmetic/control-flow model; no huge allocation or native execution. With overflow checks disabled the augmented width wraps to0 and later F2Vector::zeros rejects the huge column length. Ordinary bounded axes and exact small matrix mathematics pass independent controls.

findings.title: Generic Lie antisymmetry fails to enforce alternation in characteristic two
findings.statement: verify_antisymmetry checks c_ab+c_ba=0 and claims this includes[x_a,x_a]=0, but Field+ExactRing permits characteristic2. A two-dimensional GF2table with[e0,e0]=e1and all other brackets0 passes both antisymmetry and Jacobi while failing the alternating Lie axiom; the CE differential discards its diagonal bracket.
findings.limits: Characteristic2custom lawfulscalar model, not a claim that the existing rational sl2 examples fail. Constructors do not claim to prevalidate axioms; the named antisymmetry check itself has the mathematical gap.

findings.title: Structure table cube size uses unchecked multiplication
findings.statement: On64bitusize, dimension2^22 gives dimension³=2^66. StructureConstants::new(dimension,empty_table) panics with overflow checks or wraps expected length to0 and accepts with checks disabled; subsequent claimed valid indices have no table entries.
findings.limits: Symbolic fixed-word model without allocations/native execution. Finite ordinary dimensions are unaffected; from_fn has the same capacity product but is not executed at giant size.

findings.title: Betti routine trusts complex premise before unsigned subtraction
findings.statement: For rational antisymmetric brackets[e0,e1]=e0,[e0,e2]=e2,[e1,e2]=e1, Jacobi fails and CE differential ranks are[0,3,1,0]. cohomology_betti_numbers computes degree2value3-1-3=-1 inusize, causing checked-build panic or wrapped output. It never calls the available square-to-zero predicate.
findings.limits: This countercontrol deliberately violates the explicitly documented Requires complex property caller premise. It shows the function is not a standalone cohomology admission/validator; valid Lie algebras are not shown to yield wrong Betti numbers.

findings.title: General rational commutant dimension does not characterize irreducibility
findings.statement: commutant_dimension prose says dimension1exactly for irreducible completely reducible actions. The rational2x2matrixJ=[[0,-1],[1,0]]acts irreducibly overQbut has2dimensional commutantQ[J]. ConverselyE11,E12have scalar commutantdimension1while preserving span(e0)and failing semisimplicity.
findings.limits: The function actually computes a kernel dimension, which is useful and not shown wrong. The specialized split characteristic0sl2irreducible representations retain the stated dimension1property. No blanket irreducibility certificate should follow for arbitrary input matrices.

findings.title: Eleven Lie module mutation tests do not exercise their owners
findings.statement: The only inline tests in cayley_unitary,su2_matrix,su2,finite_groupoid_algebra,finite_path_algebra and twisted_abelian_algebra construct literal Result Ok/Err values and assert tags. They do not call the owned mathematical functions; adjacent mutation-census comments supply no executable owner control. The same literal-only pattern occurs in clifford,pauli_symplectic,heisenberg,su_n and lorentz.
findings.limits: This is limited to these inline bodies; separate integration tests or historical mutation campaigns are not disproved. Exact independent mathematical controls remain separate from native execution coverage.

findings.title: Malformed class-equation record divides by zero
findings.statement: ClassEquation has public fields; holds first accepts centre_order1 plus a zero-size class as summing to order1, then computes order modulo that zero size and panics.
findings.limits: Standalone public record is forgeable; legitimate conjugacy class sizes from admitted groups are positive. Own bounded arithmetic model, no Rust execution.

findings.title: McKay matrix silently discards extra character values
findings.statement: mckay_matrix multiplies f by class values with zip before calling strict multiplicity. Any suffix beyond the class count disappears. A legitimate trivial-group table with f=[1,99] therefore has the same matrix as f=[1], despite invalid input length.
findings.limits: Extra values alone are the counterexample; short vectors are rejected downstream. CharacterTable private construction remains intact.

findings.title: Rational cosine list does not imply rational sine
findings.statement: Finite-order rotation cosine prose additionally says with rational sine, but returned cosines include plus/minus1/2, whose sine squared3/4 has no rational square root.
findings.limits: Correct Niven rational-cosine list and the separate matrix finite-order decision are not refuted.

findings.title: Shape Lie algebra is complexified, not the stated anti-Hermitian real algebra
findings.statement: shape_lie_algebra claims rational anti-Hermitian shapes but passes the unscaled Hermitian Gell-Mann matrices to StructureConstants<GaussianRat>. For N2, Z*=Z and [X,Y]=2iZ. This is closure over Q(i), with no real compact anti-Hermitian basis admission.
findings.limits: The complex commutator structure table can be correct. This is a carrier/basis interpretation error, not a failure of the explicit Hermitian Gram or Casimir identities.

findings.title: Full PGL does not equal the orthochronous Lorentz component
findings.statement: Module prose identifies SO+(1,2;Q) with PGL(2,Q), but g=diag(-1,1) has adjoint diag(-1,1,-1), which preserves eta and determinant1 while reversing time. The positive-determinant projective subgroup is required; the actual adjoint function documentation correctly states this distinction.
findings.limits: The actual adjoint construction intentionally accepts both determinant signs. check_proper_orthochronous correctly rejects the time-reversing example.

findings.title: Public holonomy carriers bypass shape and inverse admission
findings.statement: DiscreteConnection and ExactMatrix expose mutable/deserializable dimensions/data/maps. Reverse transport can change without changing forward state/hash; malformed1x1empty matrix can reach direct indexing in supposedly fallible arithmetic. CellComplex consumers other than guarded cochain_matrices also trust public index maps. Edge-indexed gauge_fixing also trusts public vertex_map indices in edge_endpoints/spanning_forest; its private connection protects values but does not reconstruct the complex.
findings.limits: Builder-valid objects retain their checked invariants until mutation; cochain_matrices explicitly reconstructs and rejects malformed carriers, so the finding does not apply to that guarded path.

findings.title: Content hashes use noninjective endpoint encodings
findings.statement: Valid endpoint pairs(a->b,c)and(a,b->c)serialize to the same edge text a->b->c. With identical matrix values, connection digests coincide; graph digests also coincide when both use the same four-vertex set and their distinct single edge.
findings.limits: This is an encoding collision, not a cryptographic SHA256collision. It uses only valid builder identifiers and does not require public-field forgery.

findings.title: Self-loop admission breaks pair-keyed inversion semantics
findings.statement: set_connection(u,u,[2]) stores forward2 and reverse1/2 under the same key; get_step(u,u)always selects2. Thus the stated U(v,u)=U(u,v)^-1 law fails for an admitted loop. Graph permits loops, counts them once despite incoming+outgoing degree wording, and Laplacian skips them entirely. The newer EdgeConnection.step uses an explicit direction and correctly distinguishes selfloop inverse. Its conversion back to the pair-keyed API still exempts selfloops from refusal.
findings.limits: The completely reviewed edge-indexed gauge-fixing API handles explicit self-loop orientation correctly; its conversion back to the pair-keyed API still admits the ambiguous loop. This finding is confined to the vertex-pair semantics and its conversion boundary.

findings.title: Laplacian construction does not establish its PSD or graph contract
findings.statement: compute accepts arbitrary invertible transport and arbitrary signed weights. U=2 yields[[1,-2],[-1/2,1]], which is not Hermitian; identity transport with weight-1 yields a negative quadratic form. It also builds nonzero blocks for connection edges absent from CellComplex, invalidating the unconditional trace2d|E|statement.
findings.limits: The newer gauge_fixing::EdgeConnection::connection_laplacian explicitly computes D*WD and states positivity conditional on positive real weights and conjugation-compatible scalar laws; that stronger mechanism is not refuted. Legacy constructor conditions remain unenforced.

findings.title: Laplacian block orientation conflicts with connection gauge action
findings.statement: Connection transports map u to v and transform g(v)U(u,v)g(u)^-1, but Laplacian block(u,v)stores-U(u,v)instead of reverse transport. Starting from identity edge and rational orthogonal gauges g(a)=I,g(b)=J=[[0,-1],[1,0]], the constructed transformedL differs from G L G^-1 and sends the transported parallel section(1,0,0,1)to(2,0,0,2).
findings.limits: Valid unitary rational2x2countermodel with positiveunitweight and one edge. Separate gauge_fixing.rs517–627 uses correctly oriented incidence and D*WD and passes the independentcontrol; finding is specific to legacy laplacian.rs.

findings.title: Perturbation bound trusts nonnegative weights without checking them
findings.statement: A four-cycle with alternating weights+1,-1has all weighted diagonal degrees0and a nonzero Hermitian Laplacian. Its certificate reports operator_norm_bound0for epsilon2. Changing every unittransportI to-I gives nonzero Hermitian delta with absolute row sum4, contradicting that numerical bound.
findings.limits: The control violates the documented nonnegative-weight convention, which compute/certificate do not enforce. For admitted nonnegativeweights and Hermitian perturbations, the written Weyl-Gershgorin bound is appropriate. The unperturbed gap is supplied, not independently measured.

findings.title: Face flatness and arbitrary loop products do not certify pure gauge or homology pairing
findings.statement: is_flat returns true on every face-free graph regardless of cycle holonomy. A two-cycle graph with noncommuting unipotent transports has a commutator loop with zero H1class but nonidentity transport; cycle_homology_pairing returns that raw matrix despite its H1pairing label.
findings.limits: Localfaceflatness is valid narrowerpredicate. Newer gauge_fixing::holonomy_verdict explicitly distinguishes FlatNontrivial from GaugeTrivial and computes fundamentalgeneratorresiduals. The qualified Bianchi function is not refuted.

findings.title: Nested built-in Gaussian scalar is not a field and rank hides inversion refusal
findings.statement: GaussianRational<T> implements ExactScalar for every ExactScalar T, including GaussianRational<BigRational>. The nonzero outerelement(inner i,inner1)has norm i²+1=0and refuses inversion; rank of its1x1matrix silently returns0because exact_inv errors are discarded.
findings.limits: Ordinary QandQ(i)overQare unaffected. Nested built-in instantiation shows the trait bound is insufficient for advertised field elimination; a domain restriction or propagated error is needed.

findings.title: Several operation-limit parameters are not enforced on the mathematical work
findings.statement: curvature_commutator names its limits argument _limits and uses unbounded matmul. Path holonomy uses try_identity/matmul without max_dimension or contraction limits; matmul_with_limits itself checks only result rows/columns, admitting arbitrarily wide inner dimension under a small dimension limit. Indexed incidence and D*WD have genuine work checks, but flat_cyclic_gauge_classes allocates faces*z without checked multiplication or its own operation cap; trivial connection allocates identities before dimension admission.
findings.limits: Checked integer products and allocation failure handling remain useful. This is a declared budget boundary gap, not evidence that ordinary small calculations are wrong.

findings.title: Capacity-wrapper tests are not mathematical owner tests
findings.statement: The appended count/capacity BoundaryRecord tests in connection,curvature,holonomy,laplacian and matrix exercise only unrelated integer admission inequalities. Their mutation-accounting labels do not provide controls for inversion,curvature,holonomy,Laplacian or elimination. Gauge_fixing likewise has only capacity-wrapper inline tests; signed_transport and gauge_quotient append literal Ok/Err tag tests despite their substantive runtime checks. Modular.rs also appends only literal Ok/Err tests; catalog appends only a count/capacity test. These do not establish modular identities or catalog realization.
findings.limits: These wrapper tests are meaningful for the wrappers themselves. Separate integrations/historical campaigns were not run; graph cochain and functional-orbit inline tests are substantive and are distinguished.

findings.title: Root-of-unity helper falsely reports field insufficiency for large exponents
findings.statement: FusionScalar::root_of_unity multiplies k by w/n with checked i64 multiplication before reducing modulo w. For GaussianRat,w4,n1,k=i64MAX, it returns None and the public wrapper reports FieldTooSmall although the requested first root is exactly1.
findings.limits: Safe refusal rather than false acceptance/panic. Reducing k modulo n before multiplication avoids the spurious refusal; ordinary small exponents and genuine field exclusions are unaffected.

findings.title: Galois wording conflates changed pivotal signs with fixed associator data
findings.statement: The dimension prose says the same F data admit Galois-conjugate dimension vectors, and the Z2 test calls rational signs +1 and -1 Galois conjugate. Field automorphisms fix rational1. For the catalog Fibonacci F00=phi^-1, conjugating d=phi to (1-sqrt5)/2 while keeping F fixed gives d²F00²=(7-3sqrt5)/2, not1; true Galois conjugation also changes F. The checker correctly rejects this inconsistent combination.
findings.limits: Documentation/mathematical characterization defect, not false acceptance by dimension consistency checks. Alternate pivotal characters can produce rational sign changes, but are not Galois automorphisms.

findings.title: RepS3 example does not test the multiplicity-free admission boundary
findings.statement: The test described as a multiplicity obstruction uses RepS3, whose std tensor std is 1+sgn+std and has no coefficient above1. FSymbols::trivial rejects it because it is not pointed, so this test cannot demonstrate rejection of a genuine multiplicity2 fusion rule. The actual coefficient gate exists and is separate.
findings.limits: Test adequacy/label issue only. Independent RepA4 table gives a genuine multiplicity2 positive ring for a future gate control; no retained Rust tests executed.

findings.title: Unverified modular data can return the wrong Frobenius-Schur indicator
findings.statement: ModularData::from_ribbon permits degenerate ribbon categories and does not verify modularity. Its frobenius_schur_indicator method nevertheless uses the modular Bantay formula and accepts any result in {-1,0,1} without invoking verify or checking duality. For symmetric pointed Vec(C3), F=R=1 and dimensions1 pass the ribbon equations; S is all ones and singular, yet the method returns1 for both nonselfdual simple labels, whose second indicator is0. The separate verified constructor correctly refuses the singular S.
findings.limits: Admission/API boundary defect rather than a counterexample on verified modular input. from_ribbon openly documents its weaker status, but the invariant method does not enforce its additional prerequisite. Ground-state and central-charge labels likewise need the modular interpretation premise; no physical observation is established.

findings.title: Generic LP verifier omits raw rational denominator admission
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: Unlike the full Phi1 and form paths, generic Phi1Verifier performs comparisons/arithmetic on public BigRational inputs without rejecting zero denominators. BigRational::new_raw permits those values. Validate denominators before comparisons and add typed-refusal tests.
findings.limits: Synthetic 1x1 LP with BigRational::new_raw(1,0) panics in num-rational; panic is caught by the probe. No forged certificate or authority exploit claimed.
findings.validation: RFC-V002

findings.title: Floating dual-boundary maximum can hide arithmetic NaN
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: Finite d0 and dual values can overflow products to opposite infinities, summing to NaN in d0^T dual; fold(0,f64::max) discards NaN. The final finite scalar checks may therefore return a zero boundary defect. Check every intermediate residual/boundary entry before reductions.
findings.limits: Diagnostic API only; no exact-certificate or authority promotion asserted.
findings.validation: RFC-V002

findings.title: CheckedPacket compares witness values without binding their carrier identities
findings.detail: new_checked compares trichotomy.phi1_value to verified_phi1.value only, then copies arbitrary nonzero certificate refs and caller carrier/boundary/weights/defect hashes. Equal values from unrelated presentations can populate one apparently checked packet. Require source/certificate bindings or document and encode an explicit trusted admission layer that establishes them.
findings.limits: Sealed result retains FactOnly and later certificate retains None; no runtime authority exploit claimed. Parent core_policy review may supply additional downstream constraints.

findings.title: Weighted norm deserialization bypasses positive weights and evaluation admits nonfinite outputs
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: Derived Deserialize accepts weights [-1] despite new rejecting them; evaluate([1]) then returns Ok(-1), contradicting norm nonnegativity. Even valid weights allow NaN input or finite overflow to Ok(NaN/inf). Route deserialization through constructor and validate evaluation coordinates/results.
findings.limits: Floating diagnostic API; no exact-certificate or authority exploit claimed.
findings.validation: RFC-V003

findings.title: Residual constructor treats the Exact alias as a valid-rational seal
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: Exact is a public BigRational alias and permits new_raw(1,0). Residual::new sends it into a guard returning None then unreachable!, producing a panic instead of a typed refusal. Provide checked construction or a genuinely sealed exact scalar.
findings.limits: Native constructor; valid wire parsing follows a separate guarded path. No forged residual or authority claim.
findings.validation: RFC-V003

findings.title: Public splitting parameter constructor can panic when basis width exceeds ambient dimension
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: For m=1,r=2 it sets s=m-min(r,m)=0 and admits all listed shapes, then slices inverse[..r] although inverse length=m. Main certificate verify separately rejects r>m, but direct exported Result API does not. Check r<=m before slicing.
findings.limits: Malformed native helper input; not a forged verified splitting.
findings.validation: RFC-V004

findings.title: Observer gauge objects do not preserve the positive finite weight premise
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: Public/Deserialize weights allow negative/nonfinite values bypassing ScalarGauge::new; VectorGauge and TraceGauge have no constructor gate. All evaluations only compare outer lengths, so purported gauge can return negative or nonfinite values. Seal/validate weights and arithmetic, and treat supplied singular values as an explicitly unverified adapter input.
findings.limits: Representative diagnostics only. General CPTP maps contract trace distance; the source CPTP-invariant phrase is not established by this implementation.
findings.validation: RFC-V004

findings.title: Phi2/Phi3/Phi4 certificate serializers emit a shape their deserializers reject
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: Deserialize routes through Vec<String>/String wire types, while derived Serialize writes BigRational arrays directly. For valid native zero certificates in all three degrees, native verification succeeds but serialize then deserialize fails. Implement symmetric canonical wire conversion/serialization and roundtrip tests.
findings.validation: RFC-V004
findings.limits: Replay/interop defect; native mathematical acceptance is not thereby unsound.

findings.title: Bianchi and rational observer evaluators omit invalid-rational admission
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow-check modes
findings.detail: BigRational::new_raw(1,0) passed as a1x1 d2 coefficient makes evaluate_bianchi_defect panic, despite its Result signature; rational_squared_l2 also panics. Phi3 certificate verifier and Phi4 curvature evaluator have denominator checks, so behavior is inconsistent across neighboring entry points. Validate all consumed scalar families before arithmetic.
findings.validation: RFC-V004
findings.limits: Malformed native scalar inputs; no forged valid certificate or provider behavior claimed.

findings.title: Phi4 test labels a fabricated zero-map complex as the boundary of a5-simplex
findings.detail: simplex5_boundary_complex claims S4, but assigns all-zero d0/d1/d2 and manufactures d3 columns by tet%6. With d0=0 and six vertices its H0 dimension is6, not connected S4. The sole acceptance test uses all-zero flux/residual/dual, so it does not demonstrate a nonzero4-cavity obstruction or actual simplicial boundary. Rename as synthetic chain or replace with true oriented incidence and independent nonzero witness tests.
findings.limits: The generic quotient checker may be correct for the synthetic matrix; the defect is the topology/test-evidence claim, not proven false native arithmetic.

findings.title: Global Meron transport accepts off-support occupation changes
findings.detail: A two-row temporal-propagation cycle on3sites, local pair(0,1), toggles site2 occupation0->1->0 while local pair remains00. verify returns global_transport_continuity_verified=true and licenses_independent_loop_theorem=true. Projection checks only two local sites, successor checks only links between rows; neither checks that each local operator leaves off-support sites unchanged. Require row-wise support preservation before deriving local matrix entries.
findings.limits: The independent orientation character identity still holds for the synthetic loop; defect concerns accepting this as transport from the declared local Hamiltonian, not a refutation of the conditional character identity.
findings.validation: RFC-V005
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow modes

findings.title: Meron loop bounds guard shift width rather than executable work or allocation
findings.detail: 63 self-loop rows enter auto-sign verifier and request2^63 i64 weights, causing capacity overflow before allocation in both modes. Smaller admitted counts remain exponential, family verifier is4^n; input-sized loop guards do not provide practical budget. Add checked allocation/work admission before cloning/enumeration, and validate public/decoded family parameters.
findings.limits: Probe deliberately triggered deterministic capacity-overflow rejection before allocation; no large allocation or long enumeration attempted.
findings.validation: RFC-V005
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow modes

findings.title: Meron exact certificate and loop parity use unchecked bounded arithmetic
findings.detail: Two positive zero-sector weights i64::MAX with denominator1 form a valid finite certificate but partition summation panics with overflow checks and returns Ok with wrapped sums without them. LoopDescriptor temporal_winding=u32::MAX,bond_count0 similarly panics checked mode before parity; unchecked parity remains correct modulo2. Family row/site counts also lack checked arithmetic. Use BigRational or checked typed arithmetic refusal; compute parity from reduced bits.
findings.limits: No false mathematical cancellation certificate established: pairwise sign-reversal conditions independently imply cancellation. This is arithmetic fidelity/totality and reproducibility failure; overflow mode difference recorded.
findings.validation: RFC-V005
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow modes

findings.title: Mechanized locus check accepts declarations inside Lean comments
findings.detail: A file containing only a block comment with theorem phantom : False := by sorry returns no refusal for MECHANIZED. Scanner matches raw line tokens; qualified-path branch also checks namespace and declaration independently. Parse actual Lean declarations or bind checked elaboration/declaration receipts; preserve explicit distinction between source presence and theorem verification.
findings.limits: Registry already disclaims fresh elaboration. This demonstrates failure of its narrower declaration-existence check, not a forged Lean kernel theorem.
findings.validation: RFC-V005
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow modes

findings.title: Trace heuristic behavior contradicts anti-collapse and final-jump labels
findings.detail: Constant text x->x gives entropy channel0, so cannot force variation as claimed. Final jump on[0,0,1] reports position0.5 despite documentation1.0=final step; formula uses edge start index/(n-1). Structural overlap(a a,a)=0 but reverse=0.5 despite claim to ignore repetition. Also zero normalized pairing returns Ok(NaN). Correct names/docs and finite admission or algorithms before evidence use.
findings.limits: Heuristics are explicitly separate from canonical functionals; no effect on exact Phi1/Gamma2 certificate soundness claimed.
findings.validation: RFC-V005
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow modes

findings.title: Meron supported-contract parser accepts unrelated suffix names
findings.detail: math:meron_sign_problem_toy_exact_cancellation_UNRELATED:v0.2.1 is accepted because starts_with prefix plus rsplit_once version does not require exact contract stem. Parse exact stem and supported version semantics before using stale-artifact firebreak.
findings.limits: Identifier classification defect only; no certified authority minting path demonstrated.
findings.validation: RFC-V005
findings.status: reproduced by unchanged-source native probe in both overflow modes

findings.title: Meron registry claim reverses cancellation sector and overstates its listed harness
findings.detail: PO-023-C1 says negative signs cancel in zero-meron sector; actual verifier requires that sector positive and cancels paired nonzero-meron sector. FSP rows label PROVED and name phi1_conformance.rs, whose entire330lines contain Phi1 LP/metadata/authority syntax tests and no Meron checker or cancellation cases. Registry status is author metadata; replace wrong sector and link actual bounded owner/tests with physical-extraction assumptions.
findings.limits: This does not deny the finite involution theorem. Registry header explicitly says it is not a proof checker; correct its content and avoid treating labels as validation.

findings.title: Historical layout checks cannot replay current custody and one Lean pin guard silently skips absent sources
findings.detail: Current exists-only checks confirm missing code/crates_rs authority/contracts paths, historical Lean snapshot, atlas paper root and governance contract YAML. The first, third and fourth tests would fail opening/asserting these paths; the Lean parity test instead wraps three source-hash checks in is_dir and can pass without checking any pinned Lean bytes. Replace historical paths with explicitly preserved archive-backed bindings or require a typed unavailable result; do not count skipped source pins as parity.
findings.limits: Source-established path failure and independent existence controls; full integration tests were not run, and no historical archive or private file was read.
findings.validation: RFC-V006

findings.title: Both independent factory vectors fail current typed hash replay
findings.detail: Declared Phi1 input hash starts9e8a3a94 but current native and independent Python compute f91fc932; Gamma2 declared d8ce337d but both compute8b4c608f. Config/output/evidence hashes also differ. Native values12 and1 agree; both supplied records return RecordMismatch. Existing factory unit test compares exactly these records and would fail at its comparison. Preserve old vectors as historical evidence and independently regenerate current version with explicit encoding provenance, or restore intended compatible framing after specification review.
findings.limits: Direct unchanged owner source with cached dependencies, two public vectors. This is replay/conformance failure, not false arithmetic certification; replay correctly refuses. Origin of stale hash convention is not established.
findings.status: independently reproduced by Python and unchanged-source native probe

findings.statement: CyclomaticWitness accepts a false component count and consequently an incorrect graph Betti number.
findings.reason: Two distinct vertices with one connecting edge and caller components=2 pass every displayed guard and yield E+C-V=1, while independently derived connectivity has one component and b1=0. Checking1<=C<=V and nonnegativity does not bind C to the graph.
findings.limits: Independent exact predicate/model control, not executed Rust. A truthful supplied component count restores the standard graph formula.

findings.statement: Chain and Cochain arithmetic accepts incompatible bases while retaining the left basis label.
findings.reason: Only degree and coefficient length are compared. Coordinates1 in basis e and1 in basis2e add as2e-labelled-coordinate units, whereas actual sum is3e. Subtraction has the same missing basis check.
findings.limits: Source and independent finite coordinate model; no Rust execution. Callers may impose an additional same-basis precondition.

findings.statement: Chain and Cochain hashes omit degree and basis and use the same vector domain.
findings.reason: Distinct mathematical typed elements with identical coordinate lists feed identical bytes to hash_vector; no cryptographic collision is required. Existing changed-coordinate tests do not cover this.
findings.limits: This is a contextual-binding gap if these hashes identify full elements; an explicitly coordinate-only digest or separately bound carrier context is valid.

findings.statement: Construction-time chain/cochain and witness invariants are not preserved by the public representation.
findings.reason: Public map/dimension/element/witness fields allow safe replacement after verification without updating cached witness hashes. ChainComplex also has a separate public boundaries copy. Privateunit witnessfields block literals but derivedDeserialize admits wireconstruction with no predicate replay.
findings.limits: Source-visible invariant boundary; finite model shows0 product becoming1 under permitted matrixreplacement. No actual Rust/Serde execution and no claim that all consumers omit revalidation. Carrier itself is different: private owned state with shared-only accessors protects these construction invariants through its displayed API. CertifiedBoundaryMap is also private and its construction is explicitly unwired.

findings.statement: Cycle and cocycle constructors treat an omitted map as proof of zero boundary without binding its absence to a carrier.
findings.reason: For vector[1] under identityboundary, Some(map)refuses while None alwaysmintsawitness under the same suppliedcomplexhash. The Nonebranch neitherchecksdegree0/topdegree norresolves thathash toitsmap.
findings.limits: Caller-declared zero differential is a valid conditional case; the API does not establish that premise. Independent finite model only.

findings.statement: CertifiedChainMap checks commuting squares on a caller-provided view without checking that the views are chain complexes.
findings.reason: FiniteChainComplexView can expose scalar boundarymaps[1],[1] with arbitraryhashes. Identitymaps satisfyeverycheckedcommutingsquare, yetdifferentialsquareis1. This yields certification ofmaps between invalidcomplexviews.
findings.limits: The commuting-square calculation itself is correct. The missing premise is verifiedcomplexadmission, not a false matrixequation; no nativeexecution.

findings.statement: Chain-map witness hashing omits map shape and silently substitutes empty bytes on serialization failure.
findings.reason: Atfixeddegree, 1x2and2x1mapswithflatentries[1,2]haveidenticalhashinput. Anempty-boundaryview suppliesnodimensions toseparatelybindthose shapes. unwrap_or_default also makes serializationfailureindistinguishable fromemptyserializedpayload atthatseam.
findings.limits: Shape countermodel is exactprehashcomparison; genericSerializefailure is source-observed fallback, not a demonstratedfailure for the usualQbackend.

findings.statement: Standalone boundary and coboundary application ignores the input degree and carries its basis into the target unchanged.
findings.reason: An input atdegree7ofcorrectlengthpassesamap declared1->0 or0->1. Constructors do notrequireadjacentdegree, andthereisno targetbasisargument. The outputlabel iscopiedevenforrectangularmaps.

findings.statement: The dormant Massey routine accepts a generic AInfinityAlgebra but uses the strict-DGA representative s*c+(-1)^(|a|+1)*a*t. It neither restricts to an admitted DGA nor adds/checks the higher correction; it also returns empty uncomputed indeterminacy. Its embedded Massey tests never call compute and include assert(true). These facts leave the promised representative-cocycle/coset claim unestablished.

A consistent convention and substantive nonzero-differential/higher-operation tests are needed before this draft can be enabled.
