DeltaFactor does not retain the validated delta table; apply calls the live provider again. With a two-point universal zero relation, delta initially constant0 passes congruence. If an interior-mutable provider later changes delta(x,y) to x, the stored single quotient class still evaluates through representative0 while delta(1,0)=1. The issued factor no longer factors the current delta. Stable callback semantics are an essential unstated runtime premise; cache/freeze the admitted values or enforce/recheck a versioned provider boundary. This is an independent source-model counterexample, not a compiled Rust reproduction.

cycle_rank ignores PathConstructor.dimension while claiming to measure the1-skeleton. A single point with a sole dimension2 self-record is counted as one edge and returns rank1. No dimension1 generator was supplied. The helper should admit/filter a genuine1-cell inventory; its current graph calculation cannot support the higher-dimensional interpretation.

The quasi-category module is entirely disabled by cfg(any()). Its dormant verify simply returns true, without checking simplicial identities or any inner horn. Later draft composition uses vertex lists instead of face incidences, and homotopy_category_rank omits identities and takes no homotopy quotient. This is retained proposal text, not an implemented quasi-category checker; the unrelated capacity record is disabled too.

IdentityType::validate compares only difference_ref with certificate.difference_ref. A record for left=x,right=y accepts a shaped difference whose endpoints are unrelated u,v. Even structural subject binding is missing; its certificate refs also are not dereferenced. This is a shape-layer gap, not a demonstrated authority bypass.

ContextualDifferenceWitness::is_failed_transport_witness returns true from different nonempty before/after names alone, even with empty left/right/context and no differing values. Two names for equal difference values suffice. This is a reference-change predicate, not a proof of failed congruence/transport.

certify_hott_binding_table can accept six arbitrary unique concepts/URNs, provided every URN has the prefix and one is the truncation URN. Swapping canonical concept-to-URN associations or using arbitrary mechanization strata also passes. It certifies the implemented census, not the headline formal mapping to canonical contracts.

RankNullity admission accepts a reduced matrix and kernel from different matrices, and a declared column count different from the reduced width. Its count certificate cannot certify that the supplied vectors form the kernel of the supplied matrix.
findings.limits: Independent exact model of constructible outputs; no native execution. The rank-nullity theorem is unaffected.
findings.recommended_action: Derive both values from one admitted matrix, or bind and validate source dimensions/content plus kernel annihilation and independence before asserting a common-source certificate.

findings.statement: ExactRepairSpace counts an arbitrary supplied vector list as rank without checking independence or rectangular shape. Two copies of (1,0) are stored with rank2 although their span has dimension1.
findings.limits: Public metadata path only. This does not bypass the separate private ExactRepair residual replay.
findings.recommended_action: Name these fields as declarations, or compute and check a basis for a bound source matrix before using them as mathematical rank or repair-space evidence.

findings.statement: The semiring multiplication budget named MAX_SCALAR_OPERATIONS counts one unit per dot-product term although the body calls both mul and add. An admitted256-square multiplication therefore performs2^25 such scalar calls against the named2^24 limit.
findings.limits: Exact loop-count model, not a large runtime experiment. The term count is bounded and no elapsed-time guarantee is established or refuted.
findings.recommended_action: Rename the limit as a dot-product-term bound, or count both scalar calls consistently with the checked BasicMatrix owner and document per-call versus whole-power accounting.

findings.statement: Empty-axis matrix helpers weaken their stated shape/index contract: row(2x0,99) and column(0x2,99) return an empty vector because no indexed element is visited; to_rows followed by from_rows turns0x3 into0x0 despite inverse wording.
findings.limits: Independent tiny control-flow and shape model; no native memory safety failure is asserted. Ordinary nonempty-axis accesses are checked.
findings.recommended_action: Validate the requested row/column before iteration and either carry shape metadata in row-list conversion or document its loss for zero-row matrices.

findings.statement: Exact rational conversion relies on an unstated canonical-value admission at its boundary. Narrowing checks raw numerator and denominator before normalization, so raw2^63/2 is refused although its reduced value2^62 fits Rational64; raw zero denominators also reach constructors without a local validity gate.
findings.limits: Dependency num-rational0.4.2 raw/normal constructor and reduction excerpts are pinned in the control receipt. Canonical valid ratios avoid the mismatch; no native conversion or panic was executed. Generic field law premises do not by themselves validate raw values at this public conversion boundary.
findings.recommended_action: Explicitly reject zero denominators and normalize before representability checks, or make the valid canonical input precondition explicit and enforce it at ingress.

findings.statement: The characteristic-polynomial documentation extends the division-free construction to rings of any kind, omitting the commutativity premise. Over M2(F2), take diagonal coefficient blocks a=E12,d=E21: the returned polynomial has coefficients(ad,-a-d,1), whose evaluation at the first diagonal block is ad-da=I, not zero.
findings.limits: Documentation-scope counterexample, not a failure under a lawful commutative field or the tested commutative ring Z/6. No native execution.
findings.recommended_action: State commutative rings explicitly for the division-free extension and distinguish that algebraic premise from the stronger Field trait signature.

findings.statement: The centralizer-basis function and standalone Penrose verifier reset the scalar-operation allowance across phases. A1x1 generator[1] admits6 counted calls with cap4; verifying the1x1 identity inverse admits8 with cap2. These exceed the facade promise of a whole-operation worst-case bound before scalar work.
findings.limits: Exact tiny source-correspondent models, not retained Rust execution. The top-level pseudoinverse constructor has its own conservative aggregate bound and is not refuted by this witness; no time or scalar-bit complexity claim is made.
findings.recommended_action: Preflight the sum of construction, elimination and replay costs, or pass a remaining budget across phases; document and name per-operation versus per-subcall limits explicitly.

findings.statement: The LDL documentation suggests a matrix can be positive definite up to a permutation yet have a zero leading principal minor, and presents this routine as incomplete for PSD. Under its lawful ordered/Hermitian premises this cannot occur: positive definiteness is invariant under permutation and every principal restriction remains positive definite. The implemented zero-pivot/zero-column rule is the complete PSD rule, consistent with later source tests.
findings.limits: A mathematical documentation inconsistency, not a demonstrated algorithmic false rejection. The finite control corroborates cases; completeness reasoning comes from the stated factorization and negative-witness construction.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the impossible positive-definite example and state that LDL completes exactly for PSD under lawful coefficient and representability premises.

findings.statement: The Hermitian-order sample checker validates sign range on supplied samples but accepts any nonnegative sign on a computed norm. A valid Gaussian arithmetic/involution with fixed_field_sign(17)=Some(2) passes samples0,1,-1,4+i even though the checker itself queries the invalid sign on norm(4+i)=17.
findings.limits: Independent exact model of the full checker path. This concerns its treatment of a value it actually evaluates, not a demand that finite samples prove universal laws. Adding17 to the sample exposes the defect.
findings.recommended_action: Apply the same fixed-sign domain/range validation to every generated norm before checking positivity and zero equivalence.

findings.statement: The rational-budget description overstates its bit bound as covering every intermediate integer. Its checks admit operands and returned normalized values, while num-rational arithmetic constructs temporary numerators first:3/2+3/2 creates6 before reducing to3, and the operation succeeds with max_bits=2.
findings.limits: Pinned num-rational0.4.2 addition excerpts and exact arithmetic, not native allocation measurement. Accepted exposed values are bounded; the source already disclaims CPU/bit-operation accounting.
findings.recommended_action: Document the bound as applying to admitted and returned values, or use a scalar implementation that checks temporary-size growth before arithmetic if that stronger resource contract is needed.

findings.statement: VecCategory composition concatenates names without identity normalization. For valid f:X->Y, composing id_X then f produces name id_X ; f and composing f then id_Y produces f ; id_Y, both unequal to f under derived VecMor equality. Tests named identity-composition-preserves-morphism only compare endpoints, so they miss this law failure.
findings.limits: The source already calls this a category-shaped symbolic structure and disclaims stronger semantic equality. The defect is relying on its Category trait or test name as evidence of categorical unit laws, not failure of endpoint bookkeeping.
findings.recommended_action: Keep the explicit symbolic scope, or introduce normalized composition/equality and actual unit-law assertions before treating this as a lawful category.

findings.statement: CoordinateTuple<f64>::checked_dot refuses nonfinite inputs but does not check computed products or their sum. Finite coordinates1e308 produce an infinite square; two opposite products produce NaN, both returned as Ok. The numerical-profile comment about monitored convergence/error bounds is not implemented by this input-only gate. The disjoint-support L1 checker likewise returns Ok(error=NaN,passed=false) for finite x=(1e308,0), y=(0,1e308), because both norm totals overflow. ComplexMatrix add/sub/mul likewise directly wrap arithmetic without the finite check used by its constructors; adding two[1e308] matrices yields a nonfinite stored result.
findings.limits: A floating-output admission boundary, not an exact-arithmetic theorem failure. No robust finite output or error bound is established by this method; no Rust execution.
findings.recommended_action: Document the input-only check or refuse nonfinite intermediate/final outputs when callers require a finite numerical result.

findings.statement: The partial-trace refusal path computes expected=ceil(rows/traced_dim)*traced_dim with unchecked multiplication. A valid BasicMatrix of shape(usizeMAX,0) needs no scalar allocation; tracing factor2 takes the nondividing-row branch and computes usizeMAX+1, causing overflow rather than the intended typed shape refusal.
findings.limits: Symbolic64-bit arithmetic and constructible zero-area shape, no native panic or huge allocation. Correct admitted divisible shapes and ordinary tensor formulas are unaffected.
findings.recommended_action: Avoid rounding an invalid dimension upward in diagnostics, or check/saturate the diagnostic multiplication separately.

findings.statement: Smith and sparse conversion expose panic/resource boundaries despite checked-construction terminology: admitted BasicMatrix(usizeMAX,0) takes the empty Smith path and bigint_identity(usizeMAX) converts typed dimension failure into unreachable panic; SparseColMatrix(usizeMAX,2,[[],[]]) is admitted but to_dense multiplies rows*cols unchecked.
findings.limits: Symbolic64-bit arithmetic and admitted empty buffers only; no native execution, huge allocation or false mathematical Smith result. General BigInt bit/time bounds are also absent.
findings.recommended_action: Propagate identity construction errors and use fallible checked sparse-to-dense shape/allocation conversion.

findings.statement: So4 exposes pub m, so any caller can construct or mutate a So4 containing diag(2,1,1,1) without try_new. Methods then treat that value as their unchecked input and return So4; the type name does not preserve the documented M^tM=I,det=1 invariant.
findings.limits: try_new itself correctly refuses the example; raw multiplication and exterior action formulas remain valid for arbitrary matrices. Public construction bypass is static evidence, not executed Rust.
findings.recommended_action: Make matrix storage private and expose read-only access/checked replacement, or name/document the type as a raw candidate.

findings.statement: Cayley-Menger admits symmetric zero-diagonal tables without Euclidean realizability. Positive squared edge lengths1,1,9 pass that admission but yield volume_squared=-45/16, so the returned value cannot serve as a certified Euclidean volume square.
findings.limits: Formula evaluation is correct and docs explicitly list only symmetry/diagonal checks; this is an interpretation/admission boundary, not a determinant arithmetic defect. Zero/degenerate simplices also return zero.
findings.recommended_action: Explicitly label polynomial evaluation versus Euclidean admission, or check the anchored Gram matrix positive semidefinite before issuing geometric certification.

findings.statement: The Rational64 projector path uses ordinary arithmetic for Gram-Schmidt norms, coefficients and rank-one subtraction, and ordinary matrix multiplication for admission. Even a1x1 input column3037000500 requires norm-square9223372037000250000 beyond i64, so Result does not provide the typed arithmetic refusal available in the checked exact owners.
findings.limits: Mathematical complement is well-defined and formulas are correct; static operation/representation evidence and independent integer arithmetic, not native panic or release-wrap reproduction.
findings.recommended_action: Use checked exact scalar operations throughout or BigRational, and replay using the same explicit arithmetic admission policy.

findings.statement: compress_checked drains self.entries before a fallible duplicate addition. On overflow, dropping the drain removes remaining entries and local compressed data is discarded, leaving the original operator empty after Err. Example entries(0,0,MAX),(0,0,1),(1,1,7) act on(0,1) as(0,7) before compression and(0,0) after failed compression.
findings.limits: Rust ownership/drain behavior assessed statically with a bounded state model; no retained program execution. Successful compression math is unaffected.
findings.recommended_action: Compute into separate storage without draining the original until all checked additions succeed, and test unchanged state after refusal.

findings.statement: Shared Hermitian input validation checks only j<i and omits imaginary diagonal entries. Thus n1 A=[1+i] passes even tolerance0; square_checked returns[2i] and identity congruence returns[1+i], neither Hermitian. Both blocked and unblocked public checked APIs inherit this gap.
findings.limits: Exact small complex arithmetic, no floating subtlety or native execution; genuine Hermitian inputs still satisfy the mathematical square/congruence formulas subject to numerical errors.
findings.recommended_action: Check diagonal imaginary parts against the stated tolerance and validate finite/real-diagonal output under an explicit numerical policy.

findings.statement: Density finiteness admission is inconsistent across constructors. from_amplitudes/from_cvector compute norm without rejecting NaN, then use from_rho, which checks shape only. validate compares trace/Hermitian defect/minimum eigenvalue with ordinary inequalities, all of which fail to reject NaN, and does not check finite eigenvalues. Malformed amplitudes can therefore reach the external eigensolver without the promised finite-input boundary.
findings.limits: The missing pre/postguards and NaN comparisons are established; final acceptance, panic or nontermination of nalgebra for NaN is not claimed or executed. Raw from_raw and diagonal-probability inputs do reject nonfinite values.
findings.recommended_action: Centralize finite-entry validation before eigensolver calls, check every computed diagnostic/eigenvalue for finiteness and use the bounded spectrum owner or equivalent replay policy.

findings.statement: Several numerical Result APIs perform unchecked dimension/index arithmetic before refusal: density from_raw computes dim*dim (dim2^32 overflows64-bit), partial traces multiply supplied factors, get formats max(i,j)+1, ComplexMatrix::to_real_block doubles admitted zero-area dimensions, and set computes an invalid nonfinite entry index before checking bounds.
findings.limits: Static64-bit arithmetic bounds; no large allocation/native panic test. This is error-path totality/resource handling, distinct from valid finite-dimensional matrix mathematics.
findings.recommended_action: Use checked products and nonoverflowing diagnostics before allocation/indexing; propagate typed dimension failures.

findings.title: GateReceipt unit test has ownership and trait requirements unsatisfied by its types
findings.finding: lib.rs:287 maps a receipt to(receipt.fuel_after(),receipt.licensed()); both accessors consume self and GateReceipt is not Copy. The second access uses a moved value. assert_eq! on Result additionally requires GateError PartialEq and Debug, neither derived nor implemented in the scoped source. This is a source-established test-compilation obstruction, not an observed compiler run.
findings.recommended_action: Borrow receipt in read-only accessors or destructure it once, and compare error variants by matches or provide suitable traits. Run the actual test target after a separately authorized repair.
findings.validation: Entire lib.rs read plus rg of GateError/GateReceipt definitions and impls in scoped src; no native or Cargo execution.

findings.title: Public sealed observer can separate an unadmitted mark
findings.finding: Observer::separates enumerates valid contexts but never validates Pair endpoints; PairBits consults raw coverage/admission rather than guardedderivable. In a two-mark unary regime with only instance(0,[0]), Pair(0,99) returnsdifferentobserververdicts, whereas separability::separable returnsfalse because99 is not admitted.
findings.recommended_action: Validate pair domain before extracting bits or require a validated pair type; provide explicit malformed-domain refusal and regression controls for both sealed and custom observers.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK002 independently reproduces read predicates on a concrete publicly constructible pair; no native execution.

findings.title: Lexical signature census counts comment signatures and callback return arrows
findings.finding: scan finds literalpub fn anywhere and uses the first-> in the whole signature. A commented-outpub fn phantom()->Event isreported; a realpub fn check(f:fn()->Event)->bool isreported as Eventreturning. Explicit alias/trait omissions do not describe these opposite false-positive modes.
findings.recommended_action: Keep tool diagnostic-only or use actual Rustsyntax/type parsing; atminimumexcludecomments/literals and locateouterfunctionreturn ratherthanparameterarrows. Preserve documented limitedpopulation/unknowncases.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK004 lexical independentcontrol; not a native/ASTownerreplay.

findings.title: Finite context construction has no practical resource cap
findings.finding: AdmitForm accepts any positiveusize; contexts firstmaterializes(n+1)^arity slottuples thenfilters. Twoadmitteddata andarity100 require3^100 tuples. Neitherpositivearitynor an unrelated BoundaryRecord supplies a runtime budget; uncheckedcapacitymultiplication and allocation areoutside typedAdmissionError.
findings.recommended_action: Enforce explicit context/arity/work bounds before construction, use checked arithmetic and streaming/fail-closed resource results at all publiccallers. Keep mathematicalfiniteness separatefrom runtimefeasibility.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK006 exactcardinality only; no giantallocation ornativeexecution attempted.

findings.title: Positive arity costs become negative or overflow in mu2
findings.finding: arity_sum casts each usize arity to i64 and sums without checks. On64-bit hosts NewForm(2^63) has negative secondary cost; two valid large i64 arities can overflow their sum. Bounds::validate imposes no arity ceiling. This breaks the declared nonnegative arity refinement on public Item inputs even before search allocates contexts.
findings.recommended_action: Use a checked unsigned/arbitrary-precision cost representation or reject unrepresentable arities and sums before comparison; carry measure identity separately from numeric tuple.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK007 exact fixed-width arithmetic model, no native execution.

findings.title: Pruned minimum search omits repairs outside unstated engine preconditions
findings.finding: The two-instance pruning retains only deltas mentioning the target. A reachable rule-free base with six data, one unary form, instance(0,[0]), existing requirements(2,3),(4,5), and already-separated target(0,1) has four valid two-instance repairs that mention no target endpoint. No cost0/1 response works and no pruned cost2 response works, so the displayed min_responses algorithm returnsNone although the declared full space contains repairs. Engine use may maintain stronger invariants, but the public API validates only rule-freedom and max_items.
findings.recommended_action: Enforce and document prior-requirement satisfaction/target-collapse premises, or fall back to complete enumeration for other valid bases; give malformed/precondition failures distinct from exhaustive no-response.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK008 independently enumerates the complete unary cost<=2 population, preserving all four omitted witnesses. No original/native code execution.

findings.title: Closure round bound overflows before division
findings.finding: closure_round_bound multiplies n*(n-1) in usize before dividing by2. With64-bit n=2^32+1 the mathematical result fits usize, but intermediate multiplication overflows; checked builds panic and wrapping builds return the wrong smaller bound.
findings.recommended_action: Divide the even factor first and use checked multiplication with explicit overflow refusal; distinguish mathematical round bound from actual feasible state size.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK009 exact arithmetic model only, no giant state or native execution.

findings.title: Refunding followed by withheld license makes a stale replay checkpoint
findings.finding: Opening fund0 followed by fund3 and authorizationfalse appends SetBudget(3), then records LicenceWithheld using old World support at the new history length. The report rejects its own replay because recorded budget0 differs from replayed budget3. Existing withheld-license test starts funded3 and misses the path.
findings.recommended_action: Replay after every gate-side history change before constructing a move, or return the updated World from gate checking; add the refund-then-refuse case.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK010 independent minimal branch model; no original Rust execution.

findings.title: Boundary replay loses supply provenance across chunk boundaries
findings.finding: A Supply(x) prefix leaves BRegime unchanged. A later AdmitMark(x) suffix is rejected when replayed from that state, although the concatenated history succeeds. supplied is local to each replay call. This differs from the state-only fold contract of the main kernel; the boundary API must carry provenance or state its whole-history requirement.
findings.recommended_action: Carry supply provenance in the replay state or provide an explicit replay-session type; do not apply the main replay composition law to BRegime alone.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK011 independent exact two-event control.

findings.title: Public menu exhaustion is only relative to the caller-provided list
findings.finding: Menu exposes mutable items and count-based SpaceId. obstructed accepts an empty caller menu and emits searched0 even for a target repaired by NewForm1+NewInst0. Certificate docs acknowledge declaration status and World rebuilds the true menu, so no World acceptance bypass is claimed.
findings.recommended_action: Use a validated immutable menu tied to base/bounds, or name the public result supplied-list exhaustion and preserve the World recheck.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK012 independent public-predicate control; positive World guard confirmed by source.

findings.title: Tree continuation can reuse an admitted token and form a self-loop
findings.finding: Custom valid reading with two marks including token g2 reaches no collapsed pairs; continuation emits g2 because n_data=2. Admission designates the existing datum, canonical key stays identical, and attach merges to the parent. Fixed fixtures avoid this collision, but public build_tree does not enforce it.
findings.recommended_action: Use collision-free fresh token generation or explicitly restrict and validate reading token namespace; qualify quotient continuation claims.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK014 checks exact collision; no full native tree run.

findings.title: Derivative tolerance can lower the reported coefficient below its measured assembly
findings.finding: With g=0, all five measured inputs=1 and atol=1, no component exceeds its tolerated bound, assembled_m=5, yet m_used=0 and Taylor coefficient0. This is not a continuum theorem counterexample: the numerical helper explicitly disclaims that proof. It is a nonconservative bound relative to admitted measurements.
findings.recommended_action: Retain max(paper_m,assembled_m), propagate tolerance into the bound, or report tolerance-only conformance without claiming an effective upper coefficient.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK015 independently evaluates all five admitted components, tolerance, assembled_m=5 and reported m_used=0; no native execution.

findings.title: Unchecked surd products silently change exact values in overflow-unchecked builds
findings.finding: Surd::sqrt forms p*d using unchecked i128 multiplication. The admitted rational r(2^126,5) wraps that product to 2^126, so the result becomes 2^63/5 and its square is only one fifth of the input. Overflow-checked builds panic instead. Radicand multiplication has the same unchecked product pattern; factorization/sign recursion also lack typed work-limit refusal.
findings.recommended_action: Use checked or cross-cancelled exact products and typed overflow/resource refusal; preserve a round-trip square test at machine boundaries.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK016 emulates i128 wrap exactly; no native compilation or profile assumption.

findings.title: Sparse polynomial exponent addition can turn a high-degree product into a constant
findings.finding: Poly2 multiplies u32 exponent keys without checked addition. A one-term x^(2^32-1) polynomial times x has degree zero in an unchecked-overflow profile, or panics when checks are enabled. The example requires only two sparse monomials, not an infeasible dense polynomial.
findings.recommended_action: Check exponent addition and return a typed overflow, or use an unbounded exponent carrier; validate public canonical-term invariants.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK017 independently computes the exact and wrapped degrees; no original execution.

findings.title: Observation presentation admits shape-correct matrices with invalid storage
findings.finding: ObservationPresentation validates edge IDs/domain only, and ObservationMap::observe checks residual shape but omits Matrix::is_well_formed. A public Matrix with rows=cols=1 and empty data can enter a compatible presentation; later observing or inducing a field indexes absent storage. Repair certificate verifiers elsewhere do revalidate storage, so this is a constructor/diagnostic gap rather than a demonstrated false accepted quotient certificate.
findings.recommended_action: Validate matrix storage in observation admission and every public packet boundary before multiplication.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK018 isolates the accepted shape and missing storage; indexing failure is source-inferred.

findings.title: Lattice admission does not establish its declared one-or-two-local Hermitian premise
findings.finding: LocalHamiltonianTerm fields are public. FiniteQuantumLattice::new delegates to validate_terms, which checks labels, site membership and operator shape, but not support size, repeats, Hermiticity or matrix storage. A public three-site Hermitian 8x8 term on three qubits passes; so does a shaped non-Hermitian one-site packet. The validated helper LocalHamiltonianTerm::new would refuse these. This does not refute the analytic two-local theorem; its premise is not enforced by the accepting API.
findings.recommended_action: Make fields private or revalidate full term invariants at lattice construction and public mutation/use boundaries.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK019 instantiates the exact admission predicate with a complete three-local carrier; no native run.

findings.title: Evolution accepts finite inputs whose phase product becomes nonfinite
findings.finding: For Hermitian H=[2] and finite t=f64::MAX, the exact eigenpair is representable but -lambda*t overflows. evolution_operator calls cis on this nonfinite argument, computes nonfinite diagnostics and returns Ok unconditionally. The preexisting finite-time/eigensolver checks do not establish finite phases or finite unitarity error.
findings.recommended_action: Require finite phase arguments and finite output/residual/uncertainty values; return an explicit numerical-domain failure before Ok.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK020 confirms IEEE product overflow independently; Rust sin/cos NaN behavior and Ok result are source-based inference, not executed.

findings.title: Nonfinite short-time arithmetic can produce a green bound diagnostic
findings.finding: The signed RHS and margin are not checked for finiteness. With a two-qubit identity Hamiltonian, product |00>, g=1, nu=0 and t=1e200, the analytic defect is zero, the RHS expression overflows to -infinity, and margin>=-tolerance becomes true. This is a vacuous/nonfinite diagnostic, not a counterexample to a finite mathematical lower bound.
findings.recommended_action: Reject nonfinite derived scalars and state whether a negative finite RHS is merely vacuous; require the advertised time window when claiming a useful lower bound.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK021 evaluates the final IEEE expressions only; full native numerical path was not run.

findings.title: Replica exhaustion declaration drops failures and overstates traversed coverage
findings.finding: ReplicaAxiomAudit exposes public flags/counts and certificate() always emits Exhaustion with all-bipartitions wording. It neither binds the family/sample grid nor gates on all_axioms. Failed searches return at the first counterexample, so the emitted record does not prove that every bipartition was inspected. Generic Certificate is already documented as a declaration, so no authenticated proof bypass is claimed.
findings.recommended_action: Retain and bind inputs/results, distinguish successful exhaustive checks from counterexample short-circuiting, and require an explicit result verifier before presenting a proof receipt.
findings.validation: ROUT-CHECK026 plus full search-body review; native tests only cover small fixtures and were not run.

findings.title: Projection CLI can overwrite its reference receipt before detecting failed checks
findings.finding: The --write path writes the newly produced receipt before the later executable_checks_passed failure exit. A failed executable replay can therefore replace the comparison baseline. This audit never invoked the CLI or changed the reference.
findings.recommended_action: Gate reference updates on successful checks and use an explicitly reviewed staging artifact or atomic replacement with preserved predecessor hash.
findings.validation: Direct branch-order review; no filesystem mutation probe against original references.

findings.title: Partial category admission omits unit laws and total composition
findings.detail: id∘id=f≠id is admitted with one object and two arrows. The separate category_base full table certificate refuses the same unit violation. Treat the former as partial presentation, or validate the missing laws before consuming as a category.
findings.limits: No downstream consumer exploit is asserted.

findings.title: FiniteOneGroupoidWitness admits a reversible graph without composition closure
findings.detail: Three identity loops plus0↔1↔2 pass, although no0→2 arrow exists to compose0→1→2. Supply composition and laws or rename the witness as reflexive graph with inversion.
findings.limits: Unit placeholder InfinityTopos and mock global-section flags are separately nonexecuting mathematical declarations.

findings.title: Invalid minimum i8 signs panic during typed admission
findings.status: bounded source-module probe reproduced with overflow checks enabled
findings.detail: sign.abs() panics for i8::MIN in both vertex and edge checks. Compare explicitly against±1 or use checked/unsigned absolute value before classification.
findings.limits: Release overflow behavior may differ; the debug/overflow-checked public Result API panic is directly observed.

findings.title: Some private validated carriers deserialize around their constructors
findings.status: TraceDependency negative-weight wire bypass reproduced; family bypass source-established
findings.detail: ObserverFamily and NonEmptyObserverFamily derive Deserialize directly despite private fields and constructor uniqueness/nonempty gates. TraceDependency does likewise despite positive-weight gate. Use try_from validated wire as VerifiedObserver already does.
findings.limits: No authority promotion or external exploit is claimed; downstream revalidation may narrow impact.

findings.title: Manufactured Ok/Err tests do not validate mathematical owners
findings.detail: Tests create Ok(1) and Err("invalid boundary mutant") and assert their tags, without invoking owner predicates. Adjacent killed=6 comments are historical assertions, not present mutation evidence. Replace with owner counterexamples and identify actual mutation receipts.
findings.limits: Other external integration tests may exist; no assertion is made that these are the sole repository tests.

findings.title: LicensedLift natural-number correspondence fails at u32 overflow
findings.status: bounded native probe reproduced in both overflow modes
findings.detail: With positive source budget and increasing small mass, source.n=u32::MAX and target.n=0 certify when overflow checks are disabled. The same input panics when enabled. Use checked increments and checked or widened mass arithmetic, returning typed refusals; test both maximum index and mass overflow.
findings.limits: No downstream lift execution was attempted. This is a constructor-level certificate defect, not a Lean proof defect.

findings.title: Visit-tree cycle check dereferences an unvalidated ancestor
findings.status: native probe reproduced in both overflow modes
findings.detail: parents=[Some(1),Some(999)] with depths=[1,0] validates node0 immediate parent, then follows node1 unchecked parent999 and panics. Validate all parent bounds before any traversal, or use checked get at every hop.
findings.limits: Bounded public constructor failure; no scheduler execution attempted.

findings.title: Intake conflict preservation depends on input order
findings.detail: Conflict(a,b) followed by DefinitionalIdentity(a,b) certifies; reversing them refuses. Recheck all negative/conflict constraints after completing unions, or maintain constraints during every merge.
findings.limits: Labels remain caller assertions; this defect concerns even the finite declared consistency predicate.

findings.title: TolerantFloat bounded admission accepts NaN bounds

findings.detail: The digest retains only sorted vertex degrees and sorted weights. ChernParityAudit only requires125 Some grid values, accepting e.g.Some99 everywhere; closing masses are ignored. PPN window checks do not require lo<=hi and omit physical input replay. findings.title: Exact eigenvalue helper can certify a truncated vector or panic on malformed shapes
findings.detail: Matrix-vector multiplication uses a.len dimensions while equality uses zip. For1x1 identity and v=[1,1], the API returns eigenvalue1 even though v is outside the operator carrier. Short/ragged shapes or a first nonzero coordinate beyond the output panic. Validate nonempty square shape and exact vector length before indexing or arithmetic.

findings.title: Numerical Regge diagnostics omit boundary equations and state admissibility
findings.detail: Zero-potential three-point WDW on[1,1,1] has nonzero boundary residual[1,0,1] but compute_residual_norm returns0 because it sums interior only. Thermal density construction checks eigenvector shape but not orthonormality/finiteness; a1x1 eigenvector[2] yields trace4. Negative/NaN anisotropic probabilities skip channel checks and return unchanged density. Include boundary conditions or explicitly declare interior residual, validate eigenvectors/spectrum, and validate every probability before branching.
findings.limits: These are floating diagnostic/admission failures; no exact formal theorem is invalidated.

findings.title: Pairing tomography grades raw coordinates even when the pairing erases distinguishability
findings.detail: A rank-one2x2 Gram of all1/2 maps both standard-basis states to identical outcome probabilities, yet standard-basis effect products have raw rank4 and a declared dimension4 can grade Passes. Empty tables also pass gluing; declared joint dimension0 or a rank excess is not refused. Compute rank of induced functionals on an explicit joint carrier/operational quotient, validate dimension consistency, and require whatever nonempty table coverage the claimed composite contract needs.
findings.limits: The source explicitly calls this finite declared-data audit, not a Born derivation. Fixed nondegenerate registry examples are not shown wrong by this general API counterexample.

findings.title: Derivation DAG master receipt certifies fixed arithmetic tables without binding the named mathematical claims
findings.detail: The33-family master is an all() of locally supplied passed flags. In the142-node completion, every label receives the same parameterized C4 identity and affine countermodel integer; node ID is only copied to output, route counts only enter an unchecked shadow integer. The35-node tranche sums a fixed table. This can establish arithmetic self-consistency but cannot establish named DAG completeness, source/theorem bindings, independent countermodels or route soundness. Several other families use representative finite examples or assigned constants for stronger owner labels. Retain the finite examples, identify associations as supplied, and require actual hashed DAG/owner contracts and independently replayed per-node obligations before treating this as a master certificate.
findings.limits: This finding does not refute individual mathematical theorems in separate owners or Lean; the module carries AuthorityEffect None. It identifies receipt coverage overreach and missing enforcement.

findings.finding: MeasurementValue::ExactRational(BigRational::new_raw(1,0)) is classified exact and cloned into GovernanceScalar::Exact without denominator validation. findings.title: Unchecked decimal placeholder silently saturates ordinary inputs
findings.finding: BigDecimal::from_f64_unchecked multiplies by10^18 then casts to i64. Input42 becomes i64::MAX/10^18 (about9.22337), while NaN becomes zero under Rust saturating cast semantics. The function is explicitly unchecked and marked placeholder, but returned decimal carries no indication of lost magnitude.
findings.recommended_action: Keep this placeholder out of evidence-producing callers; replace with a fallible exact binary/decimal conversion and explicit range/precision policy.
findings.validation: RQPR-CHECK002 independent saturation arithmetic; no native execution or governance-bypass claim.

findings.title: McNemar denominator exponent truncates valid u64 counts
findings.finding: For b=2^32,c=0, n=b+c is representable, min(b,c)=0, numerator2 and the denominator2^(n as u32)=1. The implementation clips to p=1; the exact two-sided conditional p is2^(1-2^32). Unchecked n addition can separately wrap or panic. No native execution or enormous BigInt was needed to derive this source counterexample.
findings.recommended_action: Check count addition and exponent representation; introduce explicit work/count limits with typed refusal rather than truncating or accepting impractical exponentiation.
findings.validation: Exact symbolic source substitution only; independent executable control deferred by evaluation priority.

findings.title: Public second marginal helper panics on ragged input
findings.finding: second_marginal takes a raw slice of rows, obtains width from the first row, then indexes every row at each column without shape validation. The two-row input [[1],[]] reaches row[0] on the empty second row. This violates the crate-level no-caller-data-panic aspiration; private instrument admission does not protect this separate public helper.
findings.recommended_action: Accept a validated joint-table carrier or return a typed rectangularity error before indexing.

findings.title: Several rational admission boundaries panic before rejecting raw zero denominators
findings.finding: Rational is a public BigRational alias and admits new_raw(1,0). ProbabilityVector::try_new sees is_negative=false then sums this value; num-rational addition divides by the zero denominator or reduces it with an explicit panic. ClassicalInstrument compares it to zero and num-rational Ord reaches division by zero. SignedValuation sums before any validity check. These APIs return Result but do not make malformed rational input a typed refusal. The simplex/marginal owners demonstrate a stronger explicit denominator gate.

dependency_evidence.context: Partial dependency source review only; Cargo.lock pins num-rational 0.4.2, and core_number_theory/src/rational.rs:26 is the alias.

findings.recommended_action: Validate positive/nonzero denominator and canonicalize where appropriate before sign, comparison, sum or quotient operations at every public rational boundary.
findings.validation: Source-level derivation using the locally pinned dependency; no compiled Rust or native failure execution.

findings.title: Zero-step Markov evolution bypasses the chain carrier check
findings.finding: distribution_after clones initial and validates its dimension only by calling step in the loop. For steps=0, a two-state chain returns a three-state ProbabilitySimplex unchanged, while steps=1 rejects that same input. The declared output law p P^steps is therefore not on the chain carrier for this admitted branch.
findings.recommended_action: Validate initial.n against self.n before the zero-step branch; add a mismatched-carrier zero-step regression.
findings.validation: Exact control-flow substitution; existing source test covers only a matching zero-step carrier. No native replay.

findings.title: Selected residual minima have the wrong stated distance-bound direction
findings.finding: min_weight_nontrivial describes its selected-list minimum as a proxy for a distance lower bound. Even when every supplied vector really is closed and nontrivial, minimizing over a subset yields an upper bound on the full minimum. For d0=0,d1=0 on F2^3, true nontrivial quotient distance is 1; supplying only [1,1,1] returns 3, whose inferred radius would be 1 instead of the true guaranteed radius 0. The helper also does not itself check closedness or quotient nontriviality.
findings.recommended_action: Describe the returned quantity as a selected-candidate minimum; only use it as a distance lower bound after a separate exhaustive or proved exclusion of all smaller nontrivial classes. Keep the supplied distance premise explicit.
findings.validation: Independent exhaustive enumeration of the seven nonzero binary words of length three; no original Rust execution.

findings.title: Public GF2 matrix data bypasses classifier admission
findings.finding: GF2Matrix has public rows/cols/data and derives Deserialize. from_data normalizes entries, but raw construction/deserialization bypasses it. RREF pivots only on literal 1 while other paths use parity. With raw d0=[[3]], shape1x1, d1=zeros(0,1), omega=[1], the classifier computes rank(d0)=0, normalized augmented rank=1 and emits ClosedResidual with q1_dimension=1. Modulo-two semantics give d0=[[1]], so omega is Exact and quotient dimension0. Raw inconsistent row lengths additionally reach unchecked indexing in matmul/rref/apply_d1 rather than a typed refusal.
findings.recommended_action: Make representation private with validated deserialization, or validate/normalize dimensions and binary entries at every public computation boundary. Add malformed-deserialization and nonbinary-raw regression cases.
findings.validation: Exact independent reconstruction of the one-column pivot/augmentation counterexample; native panic paths are source-derived, not executed.

findings.title: Single-row periodic grids mishandle self-loop incidence
findings.finding: try_surface_grid admits m,n>=1. build_surface_d0 assigns1 to both endpoints instead of XORing endpoint incidences. When a periodic extent is1, those endpoints coincide and a loop is incorrectly given a nonzero coboundary row. For m=1,n=2, the returned d1*d0 has rows[1,1], so the supposed complex is not boundary-valid. For1x1 it passes d1*d0=0 but has quotient dimension1 rather than2 for the declared torus.
findings.recommended_action: XOR endpoint incidences so self-loops cancel, or explicitly refuse periodic extents below2. Validate the returned chain condition and test1x1,1x2,2x1 cases; retain checks for normal2x2 grids.
findings.validation: Independent exact finite incidence reconstruction, no native execution.

findings.title: Noise simulation accepts invalid Bernoulli parameters
findings.finding: noise_mc_planar_grid validates m and trials but not p. Lcg::bernoulli returns false for p<=0 and true for p>=1, while the receipt retains the supplied p and labels the run IID Bernoulli(p). Thus p=-1 and p=2 produce accepted diagnostic receipts for nonexistent probability models instead of typed refusals. Nonfinite inputs are also not rejected at admission.
findings.recommended_action: Require finite0<=p<=1 at the public simulation boundary and describe the discrete pseudorandom threshold approximation explicitly. Add out-of-range and nonfinite parameter regressions.
findings.validation: Exact control-flow substitution at p=-1 and p=2; no original Rust execution.

findings.title: Caller-supplied defect weight can hide a capacity-wall label
findings.finding: DefectEvent exposes residual and weight independently. terminalize_packet classifies residual but passes the stored weight to classify_wall_terminal and copies it to the receipt. For the torus logical residual of true Hamming weight2 and declared distance2 (radius0), the complete constructor yields CapacityWallHit; constructing the same public packet with weight0 retains ClosedResidual and reports residual_weight0. The quotient classification is unchanged, but the capacity decision and receipt weight are no longer bound to the residual.
findings.recommended_action: Recompute the weight from the admitted GF(2) residual, or reject a supplied weight mismatch. Add a regression comparing constructor-generated and directly deserialized packets.

findings.title: WF44 certificate formula admits a nonoptimal result
findings.statement: For the oriented triangle B, w=(2,2,2), f=(0,3,5), z=(2,2,2), the page conditions give r=(5,4,-3), B^T z=0, |z|<=w and w.z=||r||1=12. Yet f=0 gives norm 6, which is optimal because sum(r)=6 for every f. The displayed rule is not a valid unweighted optimality certificate.
findings.recommended_action: Separate signed cochain c from positive weights alpha. Unweighted: r=c+Bf, B^Tz=0, |z|<=1, c.z=||r||1. Weighted: |z|<=alpha and c.z=sum(alpha_e|r_e|).

findings.title: Non-derivability is not the right leakage contract
findings.statement: WF23 requires that no expected answer be derivable or a declared function of participant bytes. A deterministic task such as public 2+3 is legitimately solved by a declared function of those bytes. WF43 similarly needs to distinguish solved acceptance from a legitimate answer-free typed refusal. Existing packet audit is bounded lint/probing, not a general information-flow proof.
findings.recommended_action: Specify prohibited disclosure and judge access rather than mathematical non-derivability; separate solved, justified-refusal and transport statuses. Keep leakage lint as a bounded diagnostic.

findings.title: WF29 reverses soundness and completeness
findings.statement: Zero false rejections concerns completeness, while soundness says accepted outputs are valid. A reject-all checker is sound in this acceptance sense but incomplete on a nonempty valid set. Killing all listed mutants and accepting all listed valid cases remains finite-panel evidence, not either universal property.
findings.recommended_action: Use false acceptance/soundness and false rejection/completeness terminology and state the exact finite panel and mutation operators.

findings.title: Historical totals repeat withdrawn or overgeneralized source claims
findings.statement: WF27 labels 28 trials live although the corrected owner review retains eight supplied one-fixture traces; full-repair hints are appropriately disclosed but do not repair the count. WF48 universal 64/64 and 48/48 self-scores overgeneralize the narrower source accounts: the earlier workflow audit explicitly records the C049 secondary checker accepting 31/48 mutants. New counterexamples elsewhere do not themselves disprove an old finite score; they limit the soundness inference from that score. The blanket table errata notice does not identify which row is withdrawn.
findings.recommended_action: Bind each numerical row to a specific retained report edition, population and checker; mark withdrawn totals at the row itself. Keep model replies, self-scores, finite source probes and historical counts separate.

findings.title: WF27 lag-three recurrence is not stationarity
findings.statement: The formula r_t=r_(t-3) also holds for the periodic sequence 1,2,3,1. It does not establish three repeated unchanged residuals or a stationary loop. Periodicity may still justify a separately declared cycle policy.
findings.recommended_action: If stationarity is intended require consecutive equality; otherwise name and record the detected cycle and check that any forced lift preserves the task.

findings.title: WF41 representative completeness omits its invariance premise
findings.statement: D=A on one representative per class implies D=A everywhere only when both functions factor through those classes. On one class {0,1}, R={0}, A=(false,false), D=(false,true), representative agreement holds but global agreement fails. The n=299 zero-failure bound is valid only with a stated confidence level and independent sampling assumptions.
findings.recommended_action: State the partition, class-invariance/adequacy premises and coverage. For the statistical claim identify the 95% one-sided Bernoulli model, independent opportunities and stopping rule.

findings.title: Exact-sum WF4 makes the gluing diagnostic redundant
findings.statement: The displayed acceptance formula locally requires each a_i=f(x), so disagreement is impossible after all local passes. WF46 can measure a distinct boundary failure only for weaker local predicates or richer states than those same exact scalar answers. This is a scope limit of the declared instantiation, not evidence that its sum checker is wrong.
findings.recommended_action: Describe WF4 exact-sum as isolated repetition with agreement, and specify partial local carriers, restriction maps and a genuinely distinct global evaluator before an LGGR claim.

findings.title: WF18 and WF25 need explicit mathematical carrier conditions
findings.statement: No negative cycle is the finite difference-inequality feasibility criterion; an all-weight-1 directed triangle has no negative cycle and satisfies the inequalities with zero potentials but cannot realize every edge as exact potential difference 1. WF25 must retain nontrivial active plaquettes and boundary transports; local flatness does not make every path transport identity or imply global trivialization.
findings.recommended_action: State inequality signs for WF18 and retain zero-sum-cycle conditions for exact equalities. For WF25 declare certified block summaries, active plaquette checks, orientation and quotient-loop/gauge assumptions.

findings.title: Design dependencies are not executable or proved compositions
findings.statement: The 75 edges are acyclic and exactly match all Builds-on lists and the registry. Their declared reuse relation supplies no typed port map, task equivalence, execution schedule or soundness theorem. Learn and run A first cannot literally be an execution prerequisite for 44 nodes expressly having no family runner. Hash seals similarly require a trusted anchor and cannot establish semantic task preservation.
findings.recommended_action: Call these design/learning dependencies; separately register executable interfaces and task-preserving adapters. Unroll bounded loops and charge positive shared fuel when composing them; do not use an edge as proof authority.

findings.finding: The actual WF3 screen accepts a schema-valid operation saying Output the result thirty eight and four guidance records saying Return thirty eight as the total. Decimal38 control is rejected. Such an accepted attachment can carry the public fixture answer into the solver despite do-not-solve instructions.

findings.title: Injected phase gateways can split the WF3 run budget
findings.finding: dispatch_phase compares one gateway at a time and checks cap/max_calls but not a common accounting path/run/objective. Actual runner with an adapted scripted fixture factory completed both phases HOST_ACCEPTED, reported102 micro-USD against100, using phase-1000.sqlite3 and phase-1300.sqlite3. Same fixture with shared ledger stops before second call with ESTIMATED_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
findings.recommendation: Validate the exact shared ledger/run/objective/safety scope for both phases before dispatch, as WF5 does; keep aggregate accounting invariant in replay/summary.
findings.limitations: Default factory already uses one ledger. Counterexample applies to supported injected-factory extension, not vendor-enforced financial guarantees. Initial underquoted fixture correctly stopped after one call; preserved in probe history.

findings.title: Retained DDC gated status relies on caller convention
findings.finding: emit_gated_terminal takes any DdcStep and sets a trace-wide Boolean. Source-level countertrace: append a nonterminal step through that method, then an executed Terminalize through raw emit; terminal returns Terminalized. Gate provenance is not attached to the terminal step, despite raw-emit claim.

findings.title: Retained dual-harness tests overstate mutation/concurrency coverage
findings.finding: Six legacy test modules slice a mutation glob and skip entries lacking expected case/candidate keys, without asserting mutation population. C059 concurrent test performs sequential writes and replays; C051-C055 write serially and only replay concurrently. Relative challenge folders are absent at these library locations.
findings.recommendation: Treat these as historical adapter tests; for active qualification bind nonempty intended mutant populations/current owners and add actual concurrent-write controls if claimed.
findings.limitations: No legacy collection/run performed; source/import path absence is a checkout observation, not a claim about all installed compatibility environments. Checker adequacy remains separately reviewed.

findings.title: Legacy accepted arithmetic receipts do not establish encoding preservation
findings.finding: Five retained result units grade answer3 for the same rational system. Quarantine P* carries only symbolic sidecar IDs, omitting equations present in seed metadata; quarantine and carrier-declared seed strings have excess closing brackets. Raw replies include answer outside the declared closed prompt schema, later removed from parsed_response. Expected-value ACCEPTED is not a source-to-target equivalence proof.
findings.recommendation: Preserve captures as historical data; require independent decoder/roundtrip and complete stimulus/schema/raw binding before evaluating dialect fidelity. Reuse WF5 restricted preservation mechanism only within its declared sum language.
findings.limitations: Reconciles existing pilot0/shared offline-evaluator and WF6 review; these result folder IDs are a dialect series, not identical semantics to later numbered pilot folders. No conclusion about original hidden provider context or altered historical source.

Inspection-only escaping recovers851 and619 case populations with retained negative evidence.8/11 artifact pins in ownership validation differ for both current raw and LF bytes;72/74 embedded public seed prompt hashes match.

findings.limitations: No original archive reopened in this slice. Mismatch after tried LF normalization does not prove a broken historical self-hash or false test result. Catalog and XML review are bounded, not full-body credit.

The same claim_hygiene section asserts all75 were verified offline and with authentic live receipts. Current whole-population metadata does not establish that assertion, and selected historical tests/captures contain refusals/failures.

findings.limitations: Catalog claim review and state census, not a fresh regrade of all75 tasks. Complements prior numbered/shared-runtime triage rather than inventing new mechanism families.

findings.title: Malformed provider metadata can poison the frozen failure receipt
findings.counterexample: Valid ASCII response JSON with finish_reason="\ud800" and ordinary answer/cost. Response freeze fails after41 microusd settlement; catch retains the poisoned metadata, so final freeze raises again. No run.json; campaign stays100000 reserved while run ledger records41 and blocked=true.
findings.repair: Validate/sanitize external metadata before adding it to persistent records, or fall back to a serializable digest/error record while retaining known charge and explicit failure. Preserve raw provider digest and do not silently normalize mathematical answer text.
findings.limits: Budget remains conservative and further campaign admission is blocked by unfinished reservation; this is lost failure receipt/reconciliation, not cap bypass.
findings.resolution: Provider admission marks malformed text/metadata explicitly, preserves raw digest and lossless malformed_response_ascii_json; freeze_json uses ASCII escaping for evidence. Re-probe freezes provider_or_accounting_failure with41 microusd spent, blocked=true and99959 campaign hold. No final receipt exception remains for this counterexample.

findings.title: Summary accepts stale-hash and negative-cost receipt as observed live evidence
findings.counterexample: Copy a valid synthetic run receipt, change spent_microusd to-1000000, retain original run.sha256. summarize accepts it, labels observed_live_receipts, reports money_usd=-1 and complete_cost_accounts=1.
findings.repair: Require exact receipt sidecar hash and strict finite/nonnegative typed budget/timing/token/status/offline fields before summarization; validate internal seed/run/answer bindings. Preserve explicit trusted-evaluator boundary.
findings.limits: This is untrusted/corrupted receipt ingestion. A manually changed receipt is not an actual provider billing result; no forged mathematical grade or authority was demonstrated.
findings.resolution: read_frozen_receipt refuses stale/missing digest and invalid numeric/binding fields. Re-probe rejects original tamper by hash and rehashed negative cost by integer admission; valid frozen control is accepted. Coordinated data+hash replacement remains outside local custody authentication.
